files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbilityBehaviour
files.Summary: Abilities are separated into groups by activation policy. Depending on the policy, activation can proceed or is blocked. Even if the policy allows simultaneous activation, additional validation steps are taken before activation actually proceeds. If an ability has no targeting proxy (TargetingProxy is null)

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbilityBreakdown
files.Summary: The full static description of an ability.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbilityCharges
files.Summary: An ability's charges on its caster: several uses, each spending a charge that comes back as the ability's Recharge says, by default on a cooldown of its own. An ability of 1 charge, with a recharge of PlayForge's own, is an ordinary cooldown. Its Charges component keeps them with the ability as its caster holds it, and is the ability's cooldown model through them.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbilityComponentContext
files.Summary: What an ability's component hears a moment of its ability with.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbilityDataPacket
files.Summary:
Data packet for ability execution. Extends SequenceDataPacket so that abilities run through the TaskSequence system natively — the same packet flows through targeting, execution stages, callbacks, and ProcessControl.

IMPORTANT: Ability tasks must be stateless. All per-activation data flows through this packet, NOT as fields on the task itself.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbilityEffectUsage
files.Summary: One effect's participation in an ability, with per-level numbers and contained effects.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbilityProxy
files.Summary:
Bridge between ability activation and sequence-based execution.

AbilityProxy compiles the AbilityBehaviour into reusable TaskSequences at construction time — one for targeting and one for execution stages. Both phases register with ProcessControl for full visibility.

Since AbilityDataPacket extends SequenceDataPacket, the same packet flows through targeting, execution, callbacks, and ProcessControl.

Injection, callbacks, and usage effects are handled transparently:

  • Injections go to the compiled sequence, its callback heard either way
  • AbilitySystemCallbacks fire from sequence stage hooks
  • Usage effects apply at configured stage boundaries

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbilitySave
files.Summary: An ability the entity knows, in its slot.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbilitySequenceCompiler
files.Summary:
Compiles an AbilityBehaviour into a reusable TaskSequence.

Each AbilityTaskBehaviourStage becomes a SequenceStage with:

  • Ability tasks wrapped via AbilityTaskAdapter
  • Stage policy mapped from IAbilityProxyStagePolicy to ISequenceStagePolicy
  • Usage effects wired into stage OnTerminate callbacks
  • AbilitySystemCallbacks wired into stage event hooks

The compiled TaskSequence is reusable: each Run() creates a fresh TaskSequenceRuntime, so the immutable definition is safe to share.

IMPORTANT: Ability tasks must be stateless. All per-activation data flows through the AbilityDataPacket, not as fields on the task.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbilityStageCondition
files.Summary: When an ability's stage runs: always, or only while a tag is there, or only while it's missing, in the activation's data, on the caster or on the target. The compiler emitted no branch, so there was no on-hit or on-miss stage.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbilitySystemCallbacks.AbilityRefusedDelegate
files.Summary: A refused activation, with why it was refused.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbilitySystemCallbacks.GameplayEventDelegate
files.Summary: A gameplay event the entity was sent, with its data.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbilitySystemCallbacks
files.Summary: Callbacks for ability system events. Used for monitoring ability lifecycle without modifying behavior.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbilitySystemComponent
files.Summary: Manages abilities for an entity. Integrates with the worker system for impact processing.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbilityTagRequirements
files.Summary: Tag requirements for ability activation. Specifies what tags the source (caster) and target must have or avoid.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbilityTaskAdapter
files.Summary:
Adapts an AbstractAbilityTask to the ISequenceTask interface.

Since AbilityDataPacket extends SequenceDataPacket directly, the adapter simply casts the incoming data to AbilityDataPacket and delegates to the underlying ability task.

IMPORTANT: Ability tasks must be stateless — all per-activation state must flow through the AbilityDataPacket, not as fields on the task. Shared [SerializeReference] instances are reused across activations.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbilityTrigger
files.Summary:
What activates an ability on its own: a gameplay event sent to its entity, or a tag its entity gains. An ability activated only when code asked for it.

The core sends events of its own to an entity where an ability listens for them: and as an impact lands between two entities, to the killer and to the one who died, and . Their data hold the instigator as , the entity it was done to as , and an impact's as . A trigger can take only some impacts, roll a chance, and target the instigator or the subject.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbsorbStage
files.Summary: A loss taken first from another attribute of the one hit, as a barrier or a shield takes a blow before health: what it soaks comes off that attribute, unworkable so no worker reads it again, at the frame's end, and the rest goes on. A gain passes it by.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractAbilityComponent
files.Summary: A component of an ability: it hears the ability granted and removed, may refuse an activation, and hears an activation start, wind up, which the activation waits on, commit its cost and cooldown, and end, by how it did.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractAccumulatingEffectWorker.AccumulationData
files.Summary: Per-effect instance data for tracking accumulation.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractAccumulatingEffectWorker
files.Summary: Effect worker that tracks accumulated impact and performs work on removal. Useful for effects like "explode for accumulated damage when removed".

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractAnalysisWorker
files.Summary:
Analysis workers run at end-of-frame after all other work is complete. Used for death checks, state evaluation, and other post-frame analysis.

Analysis workers can either:

  1. Return actions to be queued (preferred for deferred execution)
  2. Perform direct actions via the legacy Activate() method

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractAttributeWorker.EChangeEventTiming
files.Summary: Timing options for attribute workers.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractAttributeWorker
files.Summary: Base class for attribute change workers. Workers can be Inline (modify change value synchronously) or Deferred (queue actions for end-of-frame).

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractCachedScaler
files.Summary: Base class for cached scalers that participate in attribute modification rules. Used for derived/computed attributes that depend on other attributes.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractChargeRecharge
files.Summary: How an ability's spent charges come back: what's in hand, and what a use spends. Extend it for a recharge of your own; each hook has a default, so a recharge overrides only what it changes. By default, each spent charge's cooldown runs alone and holds that charge back.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractClockChoice
files.Summary: A clock picked in an inspector, for what runs a sequence: an ability's Run Sequence task, or a component of your own. Each kind gives the clock for a run on a packet as the run starts; a [Serializable] class of your own made from this one is offered beside them. The field left empty, None, leaves the run the clock it would have had.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractComponentValidationRule<TComponent>
files.Summary: A check an ability's component stands behind, as Check Range is the Cast Range component's: shown among the ability's checks while the ability holds the component, and tied to it. The component enforces what it says, so the rule passes; no list holds it and the picker doesn't offer it, as it comes with its component and goes with it. A component of your own brings one with its or .

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractContextImpactWorker
files.Summary: Impact worker with standard context validation options. Most impact workers should inherit from this class.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractCueHandler
files.Summary: A gameplay cue: what something shows and sounds, apart from what it does. An effect's, an ability's, an entity's and an item's Cues components list their cues, each a list for each of its moments, and plays them all. A burst plays as a moment comes; a lasting cue begins as its moment comes and ends as it's over, as an effect that lands and later comes off, and a restore ends it and begins it again, playing no burst. Each hook is a no-op until a handler overrides it. An effect changed attributes and tags and nothing else, so what it showed was each game's own code.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractEffectChange
files.Summary: One change a modifier makes to an effect as it's made. Each writes into the application's , which the effect's own reads take in; a project adds its own by deriving one.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractEffectComponent
files.Summary: A component of an effect: it hears the effect land, tick, hit and end, at the moments its workers do, and a lasting effect lend and take back what it gives while it lasts.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractEffectWorker
files.Summary: Base class for effect lifecycle workers. Effect workers are attached to specific effects and react to their lifecycle events. All actions from effect workers are scoped to the effect's lifetime.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractEffectingMonoProcess
files.Summary: A gameplay mono process that applies effects, as a projectile does as it lands. Its effects come from its origin, and take the set-by-caller magnitudes of the data that spawned it, as an ability's other effects do.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractEntityComponent
files.Summary: A component of an entity: it hears its entity register, die, revive and end, and an activation of one of its abilities wind up, which the activation waits on.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractEntityService
files.Summary: A per-entity object its components share, as the auras an entity runs, , or the wait a Respawn counts down, : made the first time it's asked for, with ; stepped each frame by its entity's own time; told as its entity revives; and ended with its entity. Each hook is a no-op a service overrides as it needs, so a heat meter or a combo counter of your own lives beside PlayForge's.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractFocusedAttributeWorker
files.Summary: Attribute worker focused on a specific target attribute with standard validation options. Most attribute workers should inherit from this class.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractForgeComponent
files.Summary: A component of a PlayForge asset: a feature it carries, added in its Components section, a class with hooks into its asset's life, each a no-op a kind may override. An effect's, an ability's, an entity's and an item's components each hear their own asset's moments, beside its workers. A component is its asset's, shared by every entity the asset reaches, so what it keeps for one of them it keeps through its context's state, never on itself.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractGameplayMonoProcess
files.Summary: A mono process that takes part in gameplay, as a projectile an ability spawns. It knows its origin, the ability or entity that spawned it, and it carries attributes of its own: a projectile's speed is the projectile's, set on its prefab, by the level of what spawned it, or from the caster, and its code can change it as it flies. A role, as ProjectileSpeed, names the attribute a process reads for a purpose.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractImpactWorker
files.Summary:
Base class for impact workers that react to attribute impacts. Impact workers run on the source system after an impact is calculated.

Can be either Inline (for simple transformations) or Deferred (for system modifications).

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractItemComponent
files.Summary: A component of an item: it hears the item given, equipped, unequipped and removed.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractPurgeFilter
files.Summary: A purge's filter of a project's own: whether the purge takes an effect, beside its strength, kinds and relation.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractRelativeAttributeWorker
files.Summary: Attribute worker that operates relative to another attribute. Useful for workers that need to compare or compute based on multiple attributes.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractRespawnPlace
files.Summary: Where a Respawn brings its entity back: its home, where it stood as it registered; where it died; a point; or a place of your own, as a checkpoint or its side's base, a [Serializable] class made from this one, which is offered beside them. Each says where from its entity as it dies, its killer among what it knows, and its home.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractScaler
files.Summary:
Base class for all magnitude scalers. Scalers determine how a value changes based on level (relative level = (level-1)/(maxLevel-1)).

Level Configuration Modes:

  • LockToSource: Automatically uses the owning Ability/Entity's level range. No extra setup needed. The source is determined at runtime from the IAttributeImpactDerivation spec.
  • Unlocked: Uses its own MaxLevel setting, independent of the source.
  • Partitioned: Uses the minimum of MaxLevel and the source's current level.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractStopStage
files.Summary: A stage that can stop a hit: it rolls its chance once as the effect lands, before anything of it does, and on a roll that comes up nothing of the effect lands, its damage, tags, contained effects and on-hits, and each side hears it. A lasting effect's ticks aren't rolled again. As the hit commits it passes the value on.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractTagRequirements
files.Summary: Base class for tag requirement groups. Provides common functionality for requirement validation and property access.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractTagValidationRule
files.Summary: A rule that reads a tag, as Tag Weight does: its weight on the entity it checks, the caster among the Caster Checks and the target among the Target Checks, or, where that entity holds none of it, the ability's Local Data under it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractTagWorker
files.Summary:
Base class for tag-based workers that activate/deactivate based on tag state. Tag workers run as long as their tag requirements are met.

Lifecycle:

  • Activate() called once when requirements become met
  • Tick() called periodically while active (based on TickPause)
  • Resolve() called once when requirements are no longer met

Common use cases:

  • Show fire particles when Fire tag weight >= 3
  • Play warning sound when LowHealth tag is present
  • Grant temporary ability while Empowered tag is active

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractTargetedMonoProcess
files.Summary: The base class for following/tracking projectiles.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractValueStage
files.Summary: One stage of a : it takes the value and gives what goes on. A project writes its own by deriving from it; each built-in one reads its numbers in the hit's context, as any number field is read.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractVariance
files.Summary: How a Randomized scaler varies its value with its roll, from 0 to 1: by a share of it, by an amount, between two multipliers, or a way of your own, as dice or a bell curve, a [Serializable] class made from this one, which is offered beside them. Its numbers are read for the carrier with the variance as their owner.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractWaitTask
files.Summary: A wait's own: what it waits on, its timeout and what it records where what it waits for comes. A wait holds its stage until what it waits for comes or its timeout runs out, in its caster's time, and with no timeout as long as its stage runs.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ActionPriority
files.Summary: Standard priority levels for IRootActions. Higher values execute first.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ActionQueue.ActionFailedCallback
files.Summary: A listener of an action that failed: its IsValid or its Execute threw error.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ActionQueue
files.Summary: An entity's queue of deferred actions, which its end of frame runs. Actions run by priority, higher first, and in the order queued within a priority; one queued as the queue runs takes its place by its priority in the same pass. Each is heard as it's queued, then once more as it's done with: run, dropped unrun, or failed.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ActivationRefusal
files.Summary: A refused activation: the ability, its slot, why, for a check, which, and in the check's own words, why.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ActivationResult
files.Summary: What came of a request to activate an ability: it started, waits in the input buffer, starts in the next frame, or was refused, and why. It reads as true where it wasn't refused.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AddContainedEffectChange
files.Summary: Adds a contained effect to it, landing on its target as it lands, each tick, or as it ends.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AddOverflowChange
files.Summary: Adds an overflow effect to it, landing as an application would take it past its most stacks; it needs a stack bound of the effect's own to overflow. Clear Stacks takes its stacks off as it overflows, as its bound can.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AddStage
files.Summary: A number added to the value's size, read for the hit: a flat bonus of 10 makes a blow of −100 a blow of −110 and a heal of 50 one of 60, as the value's sign has it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AffiliationValidation
files.Summary: Affiliation: the target stands to its caster as it says, by the sides they hold, as an area's or an aura's filter takes them: an enemy shares none of the caster's sides, an ally shares one. A caster with no sides takes anyone as either.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AllAtOnceRecharge
files.Summary: No cooldown until the last charge is spent; its end brings every charge back at once.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AllCondition
files.Summary: Whether every one of its conditions holds; with none, it holds. A member that can't be worked out where it's read doesn't hold, so neither does this.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AllProxyStagePolicy
files.Summary: The stage ends as its last task does.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AlwaysCondition
files.Summary: A condition that always holds.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AnyCondition
files.Summary: Whether any one of its conditions holds; with none, it doesn't. A member that can't be worked out where it's read doesn't hold, and the others still can.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AnyProxyStagePolicy
files.Summary: The stage ends as its first task does.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ApplyEffectAction
files.Summary: Deferred action to apply an effect.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ApplyToCasterTask
files.Summary: Applies effects to its caster, whatever the ability targets, as the empowerment Shadow Step leaves its caster or the untargetable moment of Tumble's roll. An Apply Effects task applies to the ability's targets alone.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AreaEffectComponent
files.Summary: Area: as its effect lands on its target, it lands on each the area takes near that target too, as Storm Hammer stuns everyone near the one it hits. Without one, an effect lands on its target alone. An effect holds one at most.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AreaEffectTask
files.Summary: Applies effects to each entity within a radius of its caster, its activation's target or its point, of the sides it takes, as Volley's arrows, Rallying Cry's armor or Thunderclap's stun. Each is found by its position on either hub, or with physics on its layers, and takes the effects from the activation's origin with its caller's magnitudes, the dead left out.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AssetLoaderInfo
files.Summary: An asset-loader task and the effects it loads into the data packet.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AssetPartKind
files.Summary:
A part of an effect, an ability or an item on the caster or the target, found by a tag: a Poison effect's stacks, how many Fire effects are on the target, what every Burn there has dealt, the time left on a shield, an ability's level or whether it's cooling down, how many potions are in a stack, whether a ring is equipped. An effect matches by its asset tag, a context tag or a tag it grants; an ability or an item by its asset tag or a context tag; a tag under the one given matches too.

Where several match, says how they read as one: added up, the first, the highest or the lowest. A count reads 0 where none matches; any other part reads . A true-or-false part reads 1 or 0, so added up it's how many are so. An effect's Worker Value asks that effect's workers for a key (), about that application of it, and counts only the effects whose workers answer.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeBackedScaler
files.Summary: Scales based on an attribute value from source or target. The attribute value is used as input to the scaling curve.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeBlueprint
files.Summary:
Describes the basest definition of an attribute's value on an entity — analogous to "base stats" before items, effects, or other transient sources contribute. Each exposes Current and Base configs; this blueprint resolves both sides independently and assembles the resulting .

Per-side resolution rules (applied identically for Current and Base):

  1. If the side's scaler is null OR its RealMagnitude is UseMagnitude → return Magnitude.
  2. Otherwise call the cached scaler (Initial vs Active path) and project the side's slot from the returned AttributeValue (Current → CurrentValue, Base → BaseValue), then combine with the side's Magnitude via its RealMagnitude operation.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeChangeEffectWorker.State
files.Summary: What it keeps for one application of its effect.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeChangeEffectWorker
files.Summary:
Answers how far an attribute has moved since its effect began, for a number of the Worker kind to read: how much health the target has lost since the curse landed, from every source. It notes the attribute as each application of its effect begins, and answers under its : the amount lost, gained or changed, or the attribute as it was.

With above 0, it answers only on each Nth tick of its effect, and 0 on the others, so an impact that reads it lands every Nth tick: a curse dealing 5 a second, and every fourth second a quarter of what its target has lost since it began, is one periodic effect with a second impact of −0.25 × this worker's answer. Its tick is counted before the tick's impacts are worked out, so on its Nth tick the amount lost is the amount before that tick lands.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeChangeMomentHandler
files.Summary: Handles attribute change events (pre-change and post-change). Routes workers to appropriate execution mode (Inline vs Deferred).

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeCondition
files.Summary: Whether an attribute of the caster or the target compares with a number: "Target's Health < 0.3 × Target's Health (base)". The number is any kind, read with the condition as its owner. An entity without the attribute doesn't hold.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeCost
files.Summary: What an ability spends of an attribute as it's used: the attribute it names, or the one playing the role it names in the project, and how much, a number that can scale by level. It's paid beside the ability's Cost effect.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeImpactEntry
files.Summary: One authored impact: WHAT attribute, HOW (operation/slot/magnitude), WHEN (), and WHO it belongs to (retention group, for the per-group attribution surface). A holds a list of these — one effect can carry e.g. a Continuous "+10% speed" AND a Periodic "5 HP per tick" without contained-effect workarounds.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeMagnitudeSpec
files.Summary: A magnitude + cached-scaler + real-magnitude triplet used for ONE side of an attribute's root value (either Current or Base). Held by twice — once per side. The scaler returns an ; the blueprint projects to the slot this spec represents (Current → CurrentValue, Base → BaseValue).

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeOverflowData
files.Summary:
Bounds policy for an attribute's Current and Base slots. The same instance is used both at runtime (via ) and authoring time (the AttributeSetElement drawer clamps user input live) — all clamping flows through / the per-slot min/max helpers so policy semantics are defined once.

Per-policy semantics: • Unlimited — no bounds. • ZeroToBase — Current ∈ [0, Base]; Base unbounded. • FloorToBase — Current ∈ [Floor.Current, Base]; Base ∈ [Floor.Base, +∞). • ZeroToCeil — Current ∈ [0, Ceil.Current]; Base ∈ [0, Ceil.Base]. • FloorToCeil — Current ∈ [Floor.Current, Ceil.Current]; Base ∈ [Floor.Base, Ceil.Base].

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeParts
files.Summary: The part of an attribute's value a number reads: its current, its base, what's missing of it (base − current), or its share (current ÷ base). × Attribute, the cached attribute scaler and the Attribute condition read through it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeRegulationCache
files.Summary: Tracks attribute dependencies for cache invalidation. When an attribute changes, this tells us which other attributes need recalculation.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeRole
files.Summary: An attribute's part in a project: a role, by its tag, and the attribute that plays it. PlayForge's features read the roles it ships, as death at 0 reads ; a game's code reads its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeSave
files.Summary: An attribute's permanent commits: each retention group's total, in the order the groups first committed.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeSystemCallbacks.AttributeChangeDelegate
files.Summary: A change on its way through the pipeline. It's reused once its commit is done, so read it during the call or copy its ; don't keep it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeSystemCallbacks
files.Summary: Callbacks for attribute system events. Used for monitoring attribute changes without modifying behavior.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeSystemComponent
files.Summary: Component for managing attributes and their modifications. It supports WorkerContext and deferred execution.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeTransfer
files.Summary: One impact that moves an amount from one attribute to another, each side its own: the target's Agility to the caster's, as Essence Shift steals it, or one entity's Agility to its Strength, as Attribute Shift moves it. Only what the giver has moves, so nothing is made from nothing. As its Delivery says, it moves once as the effect lands, each tick, or for as long as the effect lasts, a modifier on both that gives back as it ends.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AuraAbilityComponent
files.Summary: An aura an ability holds while its holder knows it, on those near its holder.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AuraEffectComponent
files.Summary: An aura an effect holds while it lasts, on those near the one it's on.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AuraEntityComponent
files.Summary: An aura an entity holds while it lives, on those near it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AuraEntry
files.Summary: An aura: an effect that holds on each it takes near its holder, and comes off as they leave, as Mekansm's or a captain's command aura does. An item's holds while it's equipped, an ability's while it's known, an effect's while it lasts on the one it's on, an entity's as it lives. It checks who's near every so often.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AuraItemComponent
files.Summary: An aura an item holds while it's equipped, on those near its holder.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AuraSet
files.Summary: An entity's running auras: each checks who's near at its interval, by its holder's time, holds its effect on each it takes, from an origin of its own, and takes it off as they leave, die or end, as its holder dies, or as the aura goes. Two of one aura, as two of an item, are two runs, each holding its own. It's a service of its entity, gas.GetService<AuraSet>(), which the entity steps by its own time and ends as the entity ends.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AutoTargetByAffinityTask
files.Summary:
Auto-targeting task that filters by affiliation (ally, enemy, neutral). Uses OverlapSphere to gather ITarget candidates, then filters by matching or opposing affiliation tags relative to the caster.

Common use cases:

  • Heal nearest ally
  • AoE damage to enemies only
  • Buff all allies in range

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AutoTargetFromDataTask
files.Summary:
Auto-targeting task that reads an ITarget from the data packet using a configurable tag key. Useful when a previous system (event, trigger, or another ability) has already determined the target and stored it in the data packet.

If no target is found under the specified key, falls back to targeting invalid behavior.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AutoTargetSelfTask
files.Summary: Auto-targeting task that explicitly targets the caster (self). Useful when UseImplicitTargeting is disabled but you still need self as a target, or when you want to explicitly validate the self-target against tag requirements.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AutoTargetTask
files.Summary:
Auto-targeting task that finds targets automatically based on spatial queries, tag requirements, and optional attribute conditions.

Uses Physics.OverlapSphere to find candidate colliders, then filters for ITarget components that pass tag and attribute validation.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AvoidRequireTagGroup.ValidationResult
files.Summary: Result of detailed validation showing which requirements failed.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.AvoidRequireTagGroup
files.Summary: Represents a group of tag requirements with Avoid (must NOT have) and Require (must HAVE) conditions. Supports hierarchical tag matching via TagQuery.MatchMode on individual queries.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.BlinkTask
files.Summary: Puts its caster at its ability's target at once, as a blink: at the point, no farther than its reach, or behind the entity targeted, as Shadow Step does. Its reach and how far behind are read as it starts, at its ability's level; its caster's own mover, where it has one, is stopped after.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.BlockStage
files.Summary: A block: on its chance, nothing of the effect lands, as Tougher Times blocks a hit outright.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Bootstrapper
files.Summary: Brings PlayForge up as a scene starts: ProcessControl, then the GameRoot, which runs as the Game Root entity of the Forge Project the Bootstrapper names. It names prefabs for both, which code makes in the PlayForge folder's Bootstrap folder as the first Forge Project is made; without them it makes each itself, so a scene needs nothing but a Bootstrapper. PlayForge ships no prefab.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.BountyEntityComponent
files.Summary: Bounty: an effect an entity's killer takes as it dies, from it, so the effect reads its level, as gold or experience; and the killer's allies near it too, where it shares, as an assist. A death no one dealt gives none. An entity holds as many as it gives, each its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.BranchCase
files.Summary: A condition-stage pair for branching.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.BranchStage
files.Summary: A stage that branches based on conditions.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.BreakStageRepeatInjection
files.Summary: Breaks out of a stage's repeat loop (for WithRepeat or RepeatUntilSkippedPolicy). Does not skip the stage - just stops repeating and continues normally.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CachedAttributeBackedScaler
files.Summary: Cached scaler that combines a captured attribute value with a level-based scaling curve. The curve is evaluated at the owner's relative level, then folded with the captured attribute value via . Returned as a symmetric AttributeValue (same float on Current and Base) — the blueprint projects the slot it needs.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CachedAttributeScaler
files.Summary: Cached scaler that mirrors a captured attribute's value. Registers a regulation relation so the owning attribute is recomputed whenever the captured attribute changes. Initial value reads from the captured attribute's RootValue (its base definition); active value reads from its current ActiveValue.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CachedAttributeValue
files.Summary:
Per-attribute runtime state under the two-kind impact model:

  • Modifiers (transient, derived) — registered via while their carrier lives, re-evaluated on every , reversed exactly by .
  • Commits (permanent) — applied via ; the post-bounds delta is recorded per retention group in and NEVER reversed.

The formula (EFFECT_PIPELINE.md §2.1): ActiveValue = ConstrainValue( Override( FlatBonus( Multiply( Add( root ) ) ) + Σ committedByGroup ) ). Committed history lands where it was measured, after the % modifiers, so they don't scale it: 50 base × 1.5 aura + 10 tome = 85, and a 30 hit under the aura takes 30.

Reproducibility invariant: is always exactly what produces from current state — every mutation path ends in a recompute. There is no second bookkeeping system to drift.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CachedScalerGroup
files.Summary:
Combines multiple cached scalers using the active interface. Members are evaluated component-wise (Current and Base independently) and combined per the member's . Override members short-circuit other operations and resolve via . Regulation propagates to all members so any captured-attribute change triggers a refresh.

With no members, or none that holds a kind, it is no kind at all, so its element's side reads its number, as the Group does. Its Ignore policy threw; it sets overriding members aside.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CachedSimpleScaler
files.Summary: Simple cached scaler based on the owning system's relative level. Has no attribute dependencies, so RegulateContactWith is a no-op (inherited from base). Returns the same scalar on both Current and Base sides — the blueprint will project whichever slot it needs.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CameraShakeCue
files.Summary: Shakes the camera as its moment comes, in whichever list it's in, through the shaker the game gives .

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CancelAbilitiesTask
files.Summary: Cancels its caster's running abilities by tag, as a dodge cancels a cast: each running ability tagged with one of its tags, or a child of one, by its asset tag or a context tag, is interrupted, but a run in a critical stage, which is committed, and never the ability it runs in.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CantFallBelowAttributeWorker
files.Summary: Can't fall below a value: a loss that would take its attribute below its Floor takes it to the floor, and no further, as Shallow Grave keeps its target at 1 Health while it lasts, in a buff's worker group.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CastRangeAbilityComponent
files.Summary: Cast Range: how far from its caster an ability's target may be, the one range it has, read at its level: the ability's reach, an . An activation handed a target or a point beyond it is refused as Range, and targeting that picks one beyond it ends the activation there, told as Range too; a targeting task with a range of its own searches within it, from the caster; and the lab's bots cast it only once their foe is within it, each asking the ability's reach through . 0 reaches anywhere. An ability holds one at most. Its ability's Target Checks show its Check Range while it holds the component, which this enforces.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CasterClockChoice
files.Summary: An ability's caster's own time: its time scale times the game's; the game's for anything else.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ChainInterruptInjection
files.Summary: Marker injection for chain-level interrupts.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ChanceChange
files.Summary: Changes its chance to apply: multiplied, then added to.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ChanceCondition
files.Summary: Holds on a roll of its chance: a number, so it can be an attribute, as a critical strike chance, or an item's stacks through a curve. Read in a hit, it rolls once for the hit and keeps the roll, so a hit read twice, its preview and its commit, reads the same; read with no hit, it rolls each time. Pseudo-random and luck as its roll says.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ChanceRoll
files.Summary: How a chance rolls: pseudo-random, so each miss raises the next roll's odds and a hit starts them again, each caster keeping its own streak for the chance; and its luck, the attribute playing the project's Luck role, read on the caster, unless the chance gives its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ChanceStage
files.Summary: On a chance, the value times a number: a critical hit. It rolls once for the hit, as it lands, and its step in the breakdown says so.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ChangeImpactChange
files.Summary: Changes the numbers of its impacts on an attribute, of some impact types where it names any, by a Value Pipeline stage: one that commits, after the effect's own pipeline, kept in the hit's breakdown; a lasting one, on its magnitude.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ChangeStep
files.Summary: One step a change to an attribute took between being made and landing: an attribute worker's, before its commit or after it, inline or queued; a barrier's soak; or a gain's scaling; with the change before it and after.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ChangeValue
files.Summary: A change on its way through the attribute pipeline, which workers and listeners may adjust. The attribute system reuses it once the commit it belongs to is done, so read it during the call you're handed it in, or copy its . A deferred worker's actions may keep it: a change handed to one is left to them.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ChannelAbilityTask
files.Summary: Channels: holds its stage for its duration, in its caster's time, read as it starts at its ability's level, a critical section, as a cast bar fills. It kept a cast bar's calls commented out, which nothing drew.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ChargesAbilityComponent
files.Summary: Charges: how many uses an ability holds, each spending a charge that comes back as its Recharge says: its ability's cooldown model, an , which the Cooldown check asks and the ability spends through. Without one, an ability has one charge, its single cooldown. An ability holds one at most.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CheckRangeValidation
files.Summary: Check Range: the Cast Range component's check, its target within the component's range of its caster, among the ability's Target Checks while the ability holds the component. The component enforces it, refusing a target or a point handed beyond it and ending targeting that picks one, so this passes: it's the range's place among the checks, and comes and goes with the component. It read its range from a tag's weight or the ability's Local Data before the component held it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ClampStage
files.Summary: The value's size kept between two numbers read for the hit, its sign as it was.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ClampedScaler
files.Summary: A number kept between a floor and a ceiling: damage worked out from a target's missing health, capped. What it clamps and both bounds are numbers of any kind, read with the scaler as their owner, so its ceiling can be twice its floor, and its floor can scale by level.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CombatLog
files.Summary: An entity's combat log: the entries the project subscribes to, its last as many as the project keeps, oldest first; a test reads it as the game does, and the Debugger shows it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CombatLogEntry
files.Summary: One entry of an entity's combat log: when, what kind, who else, the effect behind it, the attribute, the value before and the change, its run through its pipeline, its change as made and each step it took to land, and, for a hit, whether it killed.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CombatLogSettings
files.Summary: A project's combat log: what each entity's writes, which the project subscribes to, and how many entries each keeps, its last.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CommitSave
files.Summary: One retention group's committed total on an attribute.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CompareCondition
files.Summary: Whether one number compares with another: "Caster's Health > 2 × Target's Health". Each is any kind, read with the condition as its owner.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ComponentStates
files.Summary: What a holder's components keep for it: an object for each component, made the first time it's asked for.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CompositeTargetingTask
files.Summary:
Runs multiple targeting tasks in sequence, accumulating all their results into the same data packet. Each sub-task runs to completion before the next begins.

Common use cases:

  • Select a target entity, then select a position (teleport target to location)
  • Select multiple distinct targets across phases
  • Auto-target self + select an enemy (buff self, then apply debuff)

If any sub-task fails and StopOnFailure is true, the entire composite fails.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ConditionValidation
files.Summary: A rule that holds while its condition does, as an effect's requirements and an On Hit read theirs: a tag, an attribute, a level, a comparison of numbers, or any condition of your own. It's read against the activation, its caster and its ability's level and Local Data, with the entity its list hands it as the target: the target among the Target Checks, and the caster itself among the Caster Checks. With no condition, it holds.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ConditionalScaler
files.Summary: One number where a condition holds, and another where it doesn't: "−0.1 × Target's Health (base) if Target's Health < 0.3 × Target's Health (base), else 0". The condition is a class read against the number's context, so a project adds its own (), and each branch is a number of any kind, read with the scaler as its owner. With no condition, it reads its False branch.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ConstantImpacter
files.Summary:
A precomputed-magnitude impacter. Used for synthetic deltas where there's no scaler pipeline to evaluate — e.g. auto-scale propagation, tracked-impact reversal on container removal, or external systems that just want to push a number into the attribute aggregator while still being a first-class carrier.

Construct one impacter per (operation, slot) pair you want to contribute. To express a (current=+10, base=+5) Add delta as a single carrier, hand that carrier two s — one per slot.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ConstantScaler
files.Summary: Returns a constant value regardless of level. Useful for fixed bonuses or base values.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ConsumeItemTask
files.Summary: Uses up items its caster holds, as a potion's use does: the Healing Salve's ability ends with it, after its heal, and the last one used, the item and its ability go. Its item system's Item Consumed hears it, so a game's own bookkeeping, as a shop's stock, follows.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ContainedEffects
files.Summary: The contained effects of one policy, read from the packets as they are walked.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ContainedSeries
files.Summary: An effect another contains, read level by level, with when it lands.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CreateMonoProcessAbilityTask.ESpawnPoint
files.Summary: Where a spawned process appears.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CreateMonoProcessAbilityTask
files.Summary: Spawns mono processes, as a projectile, as the ability runs. What it spawns takes the ability as its origin, so the effects it applies are the caster's at the ability's level, and its attributes can start as the caster's. It spawns the processes the activation's data holds under , or, where the data holds none or is on, its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CrowdControlRule
files.Summary: One crowd control rule: while its holder carries a tag, it can't use what the rule stops.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CrowdControlRules
files.Summary: Crowd control: the rules an entity's abilities follow, each a tag and what it stops, so no ability has to list Stunned among the tags it avoids. While its holder carries a rule's tag, an ability the rule stops is refused, and one running is interrupted, as a stun breaks a channel; an ability can ignore a rule by its tag. An entity names its rules, or takes the project's.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CueContext
files.Summary: What a cue plays for: the entity it plays on, what raised it and why, and where. An effect's cue has its spec, and for a tick, how many executed; another's has its origin, as an ability's spec or an item's, and the activation's data where there is one. A lasting cue's beginning and its end share a key.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CueLibrary
files.Summary: A project's cue library: what each cue tag plays. A Cue Tag cue, listed on an effect or a Cues component, plays the library's route for its tag: the tag's own, or else its nearest parent's, and a route that doesn't override plays its parent's too, as Unreal's GameplayCueManager routes its GameplayCue tags. An entity's Cue Receiver plays a tag its own way first. The project names its library in its settings, or code gives one to .

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CuePackets
files.Summary: The data a cue's process or sequence runs with, loaded for what raised it. An ability's cue starts from its activation's packet: its targets, its targeting data and the numbers its caller set. On it go the cue itself (), its asset () and its spec (), its source, the one it plays on as its target where the packet names none, where it plays, and its owner's clock; then the asset's Local Data, its numbers read for the cue, as at its level; then the cue's own Data list. Each step's keys take the place of an earlier step's, so the cue's own data has the last word.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CuePlace
files.Summary: One place a cue plays at: where, which way, what it follows, and the entity it's at.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CuePlacement
files.Summary: Where a cue places what it plays: on the one it's on, its source, an ability's target or each of its targets, or at the cue's point; at a socket of theirs, as a hand; moved by an offset in their space and scattered by a random amount; following them or not; and facing their way, the cue's normal, or from or toward its source.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CuePoolInstantiator
files.Summary: Makes a MonoBehaviour process's object from the cue pool, , and gives it back as the process ends, as a pooled Process cue's: an object of the process's prefab waiting there is handed out, else one is made, placed where the process's packet says. Give it to a registration with .

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CueRaise
files.Summary: One raise of a list of cues, as a sink is asked of it: the cue, and what the list belongs to.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CueReceiverEntityComponent
files.Summary: Cue Receiver: plays cue tags its own way for its entity, as a golem's hits, before the project's cue library does, as Unreal's actors handle cues through their GameplayCue interface. Its own routes play first; where it plays nothing for a tag, or passes it through, the library's route plays, its Variant's where the library has one, as Cue.Hit.Golem for Cue.Hit. An entity holds one at most.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CueRoute
files.Summary: A cue tag's route: the handlers that play for it, and whether they play in place of its parent's.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CueSource
files.Summary: What a raise's list of cues belongs to: an effect, an ability, an entity or an item, by its asset; a cue tag; or a game's own code. A network layer names it by the asset's ID, or the tag's, in place of the cues themselves.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CuesAbilityComponent
files.Summary: Cues: what an ability shows and sounds at its moments, on its caster: as an activation starts, as it pays its cost and starts its cooldown, while it's active, as it ends, and as one is refused. A stage's exact moment plays through a Play Cue task. An ability holds one at most.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CuesEffectComponent
files.Summary: Cues: what an effect shows and sounds at its moments, on the one it's on: as it lands, as an application it takes in lands, as each of its ticks executes, as an impact it deals lands, as it comes off, while it lasts, as an application of it is refused, and as its stacks change. An effect holds one at most.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CuesEntityComponent
files.Summary: Cues: what an entity shows and sounds at its moments: as it comes into the game, dies and comes back, and, While Tagged, for as long as it holds a tag, as stars over its head while it's Stunned. An entity holds one at most.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CuesItemComponent
files.Summary: Cues: what an item shows and sounds on its holder: as it's equipped, while it's equipped, and as it's used, as an ability it lends is. A load that puts an equipped item back begins its lasting cues and plays no burst. An item holds one at most.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DashTask
files.Summary: Moves its caster toward its ability's target, or away from it, over a moment, as Tumble's roll. Its distance and duration are read as it starts, at its ability's level; it moves along the ground by its caster's time, a critical section, holding its caster's own mover, where it has one, while it moves. A caster with no object in the scene doesn't move.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DataWrapper
files.Summary: One entry of an asset's or an entity's Local Data: a value under a key. Its value is a class, a kind of its own: a number that can scale, a whole number, a string, a bool, a tag, an attribute, an effect, an ability, an entity, an object, a MonoBehaviour or a ScriptableObject; or a kind of your own, as a point or a colour, a [Serializable] class made from or , which is offered beside them. Each entry saves its own value alone.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DelayTask
files.Summary: Waits: holds its stage for its delay, in its caster's time, read as it starts at its ability's level.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DelegateSequenceTask
files.Summary: Wraps a delegate as a sequence task.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DelegateSyncTask
files.Summary: Wraps a delegate as a sync-first sequence task implementing the unified ISequenceTask. Step is the primary execution path; Execute bridges by looping Step with per-frame yields.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DeriveScalerName
files.Summary: When placed on a Scaler field inside a ScalableFloat, the scaler drawer will look up the parent property's ScalerOperationKeyword attribute and use "{Keyword} Scaler" as the display name.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DisjointProxyTaskBehaviour
files.Summary: A disjoint, as in Dota: the shots already aimed at an entity lose it, fly on to where it stood, and land on nothing. A shot is found through the intent it registers with its target, which only a homing shot does (), and only one whose data marks it is disjointed. A skill shot, one that hits whatever it crosses, registers no intent, and lands as usual.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DisjointTarget
files.Summary: The placeholder a disjointed shot is aimed at instead of its entity. It stays where the entity stood, has no tags, and takes no effects, so the shot lands on nothing.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DurationChange
files.Summary: Changes how long it lasts: its time multiplied, then more added. Its ticks spread over the time it has.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAbilityEffectRole
files.Summary: How an effect participates in an ability.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAbilityEnd
files.Summary: How an ability's activation ended.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAbilityLinkMode
files.Summary: Defines how an ability is linked to its level provider.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAbilityPart
files.Summary: What an Asset Part number reads of an ability.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAbilityStageConditionSubject
files.Summary: Where a stage's condition looks for its tag.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAbilityTriggerSource
files.Summary: What sets an ability off on its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EActivationRefusal
files.Summary: Why an activation was refused, or None where it wasn't: it activated, waits in the input buffer, or starts next frame. A refused activation said only false.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EActivationStatus
files.Summary: What came of a request to activate an ability.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAddBehaviour
files.Summary: Cross-carrier composition strategies for impacters. This is intentionally distinct from per-effect stacking policy: stacking decides how the SAME effect re-applies stack against itself, while MultiplyBehaviour decides how DIFFERENT carriers' multiply contributions to the SAME attribute slot compose.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAffiliationFilter
files.Summary: Whom a search or a check takes, by how each stands to its caster, or to an aura's holder: an enemy shares none of its sides, an ally shares one, and the caster itself is an ally of itself and no one's enemy. The one choice an Area Effect, an effect's area, a spread, an aura, the auto-target tasks and an Affiliation check make. A caster with no sides takes every other one as its ally and its enemy alike.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAreaCentre
files.Summary: Where an area search is measured from.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAssetPartAmong
files.Summary: How an Asset Part number reads one value from several that match.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAssetPartOf
files.Summary: What an Asset Part number looks for on an entity.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAttributeChangeWhat
files.Summary: What an Attribute Change worker answers about its attribute.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAttributeRead
files.Summary: How × Attribute reads its attribute.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAttributeRole
files.Summary: What an attribute is, which sets how bonuses to it add up and how a number reads it by default, as how several effects' Damage Amplification adds up and how an attack's scaler reads it. An effect's impact can add up its own way, and a number can read it its own way.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAttributeSetLinkMode
files.Summary: Defines how an AttributeSet's level range is sourced.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EChangeStepKind
files.Summary: What a step of a change to an attribute was.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECombatLogKind
files.Summary: What a combat log entry is.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECombatLogRecords
files.Summary: What an entity's combat log writes, as the project subscribes to it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECrowdControlStops
files.Summary: What a crowd control rule stops.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECueAt
files.Summary: Whom a cue places what it plays on.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECueAttach
files.Summary: Whether what a cue places follows what it's placed at.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECueEvent
files.Summary: How a cue plays: a burst, or a lasting cue's beginning or its end.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECueFacing
files.Summary: Which way what a cue places faces.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECueMoment
files.Summary: What raised a cue: one of an effect's moments, an ability's, an entity's or an item's, or a game's own code.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECueSource
files.Summary: What a raise's list of cues belongs to.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECurveTangentMode
files.Summary: Runtime-safe mirror of the editor tangent modes used by scaler curves.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EDeathPolicy
files.Summary: What an entity's death does.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectCategory
files.Summary: The kinds of effect a death can keep whatever their tiers.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectJournalKind
files.Summary: What an effect journal's entry tells.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectLinkMode
files.Summary: Defines how an effect is linked to its level provider.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectPart
files.Summary: What an Asset Part number reads of an effect.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectRecipient
files.Summary: Whom an effect another lands lands on: a contained effect, an overflow's, or one a modifier adds.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectRefusal
files.Summary: Why an effect didn't land on an entity, as the entity's callbacks tell it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectTargetScope
files.Summary: Who an effect application lands on, as statically determinable.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectWorkerHook
files.Summary: The moment of its effect an effect worker heard.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEventRecipient
files.Summary: Whom a Send Event task sends to: its caster, or each of its activation's targets.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EFacingCheck
files.Summary: Which way a Facing check looks.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EFloatingValue
files.Summary: Where a floating text's number comes from.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EGroupOperation
files.Summary: How a Group's member joins the others: an impact's four operations, in their order, so a member saved before keeps its meaning, and Divide.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EGroupOverflowPolicy
files.Summary: What happens when a new member tries to join a full group.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EImpactDelivery
files.Summary:
How an impact entry rides its carrier's lifecycle. Delivery IMPLIES the contribution kind — there is deliberately no independent "retained?" switch to get wrong:

  • → Modifier (transient, derived). Registered while the carrier is present, re-evaluated on every recompute, reversed automatically and exactly when the carrier is removed. Only valid on durational/infinite carriers.
  • → Commit (permanent). One commit at application time. Never reversed. This is what an Instant effect is.
  • → Commit (permanent) once per execute tick. Never reversed. Requires a carrier with periodic ticks enabled.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EItemLinkMode
files.Summary: Defines how an item is linked to its level provider.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EItemPart
files.Summary: What an Asset Part number reads of an item.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EJournalActionState
files.Summary: Where an action a worker queued stands.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ELocalDataFrom
files.Summary: Whose Local Data a Local Data number reads.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EModifierDirection
files.Summary: Which effects a modifier changes: those its holder applies, those landing on it, or both.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EOnHitTo
files.Summary: Whom an On Hit's effects land on.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EProcessAttributeStart
files.Summary: Where a process's own attribute starts.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EProcessRegistrationRefusal
files.Summary: Why ProcessControl refused a registration, or None when it took the process.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EPurgeRelation
files.Summary: Whom a purge takes the effects of, by who applied each, against the one purged.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ERetentionGroupRead
files.Summary: Which of an attribute's retention groups a read takes.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ESavedOrigin
files.Summary: The kinds of origin a save tells apart.

files.Summary: Whose side a worker ran on: the entity its effect is on, or the one that dealt the hit, as an effect's workers hear its hits on their dealer's side and impact workers run for their dealer.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EachChargeRecharge
files.Summary: Each spent charge comes back on a cooldown of its own, run alongside the others: the default.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbilityBehaviourDrawer
files.Summary: An ability's behaviour drawn whole, as an asset or a component of the user's own holds one: Unity's foldout of the fields the ability inspector shows of it, its targeting, its asset loaders, what cancels it and what it blocks, and its stages. The lists are Unity's, where a new loader starts empty and each stage keeps its fold as one is removed or dragged; Implicit Tag shows under Use Implicit Targeting while it's on. It drew colored sections that folded, lists of its own, and badges.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbilityDrawer
files.Summary: A reference to an ability: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbilityEditor
files.Summary: The Ability inspector: Identity, Leveling, Tags, the ability's Activation and Stages, Requirements, Workers and Local Data, then Used By. A collapsed section shows one line, and the inspector takes its look from the style sheet.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbilityStageConditionDrawer
files.Summary: A stage's condition: its tag, a tag field in the label column, and, once it names one, where the stage looks for it and whether it runs while the tag is missing instead, each indented under it. With no tag, the stage always runs, and Unity's foldout showed all three.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbilityTagRequirementsDrawer
files.Summary: An ability's tag requirements, as the same table: the caster's, the caster's while the ability runs, and the target's, each with what it requires and what it must not have.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbilityTaskBehaviourStageDrawer
files.Summary:
An ability's stage: a foldout row named by its place, as "Stage 1", with Critical on its right while a task commits the ability to it; folded, one line of what it holds, as "2 tasks · All · Applies usage effects"; open, its completion policy, its usage effects, its condition, what cancels it and what it blocks, then its tasks in Unity's reorderable list, where a new task starts empty. The stages' own list removes a stage.

It drew a colored badge for the stage's number, its policy, its usage effects, its task count and a critical task, ▶ and ▼ as text, a delete button, and a list of its own with ▲, ▼ and × buttons, from 163 styles set in C#; and it grew that list as an array, which gave a new task the last one's object, so the two were one.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbilityTaskDrawer
files.Summary: An ability task: its kind, as "Delay" for a DelayTask, then the kind's own fields. The base drawer names a kind without "AbilityTask" or "Task", and builds the fields again as the kind changes, which this drawer did itself.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbilityValidationRuleDrawer
files.Summary: An ability's validation rule: its kind, as its [ForgeMenu] names it or named without "ValidationRule" or "Validation", then the kind's own fields. A rule is always of some kind, so the picker offers no None. Each list is offered the kinds of its side, the Caster Checks a caster's and the Target Checks a target's, with those of either; a check a component stands behind, as Check Range, is offered to neither, as it comes with its component.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbstractComponentDrawer<T>
files.Summary: A component: its kind, always of some kind, then its fields. A kind that allows one is offered while the list it's in holds none of it, the element that holds it still naming it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbstractForgeObjectDrawer<T>
files.Summary: A reference to a PlayForge asset, or to a Value Pipeline, Crowd Control Rules or Effect Modifier: Unity's object field, with its type's icon, and beside it a plain button, Open while it names an asset, which shows the asset in a window of its own, or New while it's empty, which asks for a new one's name in The Forge's New dialog, makes it where The Forge makes its type and uses it. A drawer adds its own actions to the field's right-click menu. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own, with hover colors and Clear and Open icon buttons set in C#.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbstractGenericDrawer<T>
files.Summary: A kind field that folds, as an attribute set element does: a row with the arrow and the kind field, then the kind's fields; folded, one line of their values in secondary text, as "Strength 2 · Duration 0.5". Whether it's folded is kept with the object the field holds, so it follows the object through its list. It drew colored badges for a folded field's values, and its arrow and its look from styles set in C#.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbstractMonoProcessEditor
files.Summary:
A Mono Process's inspector: a Process section of Unity's fields, its lifecycle, its timing, how it's ordered as it steps, how it's made, and whether it follows its siblings, each choice saying what it does in its field's tooltip; then the component's own fields. Priority Method shows while the process steps, and Priority under it while the method is Manual. It drew a tinted box, a gray hint in 10 px under each field, set 50 ms after it drew, and a gray rule.

Every field is a PropertyField bound to its property, so a multiple selection edits each process, and a prefab instance's edits show as overrides. Without [CanEditMultipleObjects] the Inspector never offered one.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbstractTypeRefDrawer<T>
files.Summary:
A [SerializeReference] field of an abstract type: Unity's field, its label in the label column, the kind it holds named in its box, which opens Unity's searchable dropdown of the kinds it can hold; then the kind's own fields, each Unity's, indented under it. A pick makes a new object of the kind for each selected asset, by the kind's constructor so its initializers run, as one Undo step; drawing writes nothing.

Every element of a list shares one drawer, so each field keeps its state in its own elements. The drawer kept the last element's fields and kind in fields of its own, so an edit to one element could fill another with its fields. It drew a button that opened a list in tinted boxes, and the kind's fields in a box with an orange left border.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbstractWorkerDrawer<T>
files.Summary: A worker: its kind, always of some kind, then its fields, folding to a line of their values.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AlignedFoldoutDrawer
files.Summary: Each class PlayForge serializes in a field with no drawer of its own, drawn as a foldout of its fields, its arrow in line with the rows around it, as a list's is: an attribute read's retention groups, as an × Attribute scaler's Groups, a turn to face's settings, an asset's definition and tags, a list's entries. Unity hangs an inspector foldout's arrow 12 px into the margin, to the left of a list's arrow and, in a scaler's block, out to the block's edge; this one keeps the lists' column, as pf-foldout--aligned sets in PlayForge.uss. A class opts in with a of its type here. A field marked shows only while the field it names says so, as a read's Groups shows only for the reads that name groups. An inspector drawn with IMGUI gets the same foldout.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeConstraintsDrawer
files.Summary: An attribute's constraints: Auto Clamp, Scale With Base and Rounding, Unity's fields in the label column, with Snap Interval indented under Rounding while it snaps. They sat in a tinted, rounded box with a yellow left border, under a 10 px bold heading with colored letter badges, from styles set in C#.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeCostDrawer
files.Summary: An ability's attribute cost: the attribute it spends, or, where it names none, the role whose attribute it spends, and how much.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeDrawer
files.Summary: A reference to an attribute: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeImpactEntryDrawer
files.Summary: One of an effect's additional impacts: a foldout row with its attribute and a Remove button, and while it's folded one line such as "Mana −10 · Continuous"; open, its operation, magnitude and delivery, then its order, retention group and impact types. Its Delivery offers what the effect's duration can make, and a help box says when the one it names can't happen. An impact entry had no drawer, so an effect couldn't be given a second impact.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeOverflowDataDrawer
files.Summary: An attribute's bounds: the policy, then the floor and the ceiling it reads, each indented under it, as a field that depends on another is. A bound's right-click menu sets it to no limit. It drew the floor and ceiling with 10 px labels and buttons in an accent color, from styles set in C#, and showed them 50 ms after it drew.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeRoleDrawer
files.Summary: A project's role on one row: its tag, then the attribute that plays it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeSetDrawer
files.Summary: A reference to an attribute set: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeSetEditor
files.Summary: The Attribute Set inspector: Identity, Leveling, the set's Attributes, Sub-Sets and Collision Settings, then All Attributes, the table of what the set gives an entity, then Workers, Local Data and Used By. A collapsed section shows one line, and the inspector takes its look from the style sheet.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeSetElementDrawer
files.Summary:
An attribute set element: a foldout row with the attribute, and while it's folded one line of what it starts at; open, what it starts at at each level, then Base and Current, each a magnitude field as an effect's are, then its bounds, its constraints, its retention group and its collision.

What it starts at is worked out by the runtime (): a stand-in entity at each level of the set it's previewed in, with the set's sub-sets. A note says when another element's value is the one used, and a message when a scaler reads an attribute the set doesn't give. The element showed its magnitudes as a formula, as "10 + Level", and Current and Base one at a time on a switch.

It writes nothing while it draws, and only a typed magnitude is kept within the bounds, as part of the same edit.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeStartValues.Result
files.Summary: What a set's attributes start at, over its levels.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeStartValues.Start
files.Summary: One attribute's start: its value at each level, and the elements that give it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeStartValues
files.Summary: What each attribute an entity built from an attribute set starts at, at each of the set's levels, worked out as the runtime works it out: a stand-in entity at the level, whose attribute system is set up from the set as the GAS sets one up, with the set's sub-sets and collisions, and each element's scalers, bounds and rounding. Nothing else acts on the stand-in, no worker, effect or item, so a value is the one the set gives before anything changes it. A set that another holds starts as part of it, so its values can be worked out in each set that holds it, and the attribute set inspector previews a set in one of them ().

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeTransferDrawer
files.Summary: An effect's transfer: when it moves, who gives and of what, who gets and in what, which of the values, and how much, each a field of its own as an attribute cost's are.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeValueDrawer
files.Summary: An attribute value: its label in the label column, then its Current and Base side by side. It drew "Cur" and "Base" in 9 px text with a slash between them, from styles set in C#.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AuraEntryDrawer
files.Summary: An aura's fields, drawn where it's held, as an Aura component's own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AvoidRequireTagGroupDrawer
files.Summary: A requirement group of its own, as a targeting task's or a template's: the same table, of one row named by the field, with what it requires and what it must not have; a cell opens its list, with the group's name and template under it. It drew a tinted box with green and red stripes, colored count badges, a Name and an Import of its own, and rebuilt itself as it opened.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.BasePlayForgeEditor
files.Summary: Base class for all PlayForge asset inspectors: a header with the asset's name and type, and the content below it. The content scrolls in the Inspector's own scroll view, and the header stays at its top.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.BuildVerification
files.Summary: Headless player-build verification (asset-store readiness / CI): Unity -batchmode -nographics -projectPath <proj> -executeMethod FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.BuildVerification.BuildWindowsPlayer Exit codes: 0 = build succeeded, 1 = build failed, 3 = exception. Proves the runtime assembly compiles and links in a real player (no editor-only leaks).

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.CachedMagnitudeModifierGroupMemberDrawer
files.Summary: A Scaler Group's member, cached or not, as Unity's fields: how its result combines with the members' before it, then its scaler, whose own drawer shows its kind and its settings. It drew a stripe and a symbol in the operation's color, the scaler's kind beside them, and, for a cached member, a "CACHED" badge.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ChanceRollDrawer
files.Summary: How a chance rolls, as Unity's foldout of its fields: Pseudo-Random, Own Luck, and Luck while Own Luck is on, where it's read; without it the project's Luck role is read, so Luck is hidden.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ChargeRechargeDrawer
files.Summary: An ability's Recharge: its kind, named without "Recharge", as Each Charge or All At Once, or one of your own, then the kind's own fields. A recharge is always of some kind, so the picker offers no None.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ClockChoiceDrawer
files.Summary: A clock picked in an inspector, as an ability's Run Sequence task's Clock: its kind, Caster's, Game's, Unscaled or Scaled, or one of your own, then the kind's own fields, as Scaled's Scale and the clock it scales. None leaves the run the clock it would have had.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ConditionDrawer
files.Summary: A condition field, as a Conditional scaler's When, drawn as a scaler field is: its name and its kind, picked from the conditions there are, a project's own among them, its one line, as "Target's Health < 0.3 × Target's Health (base)", then the condition's own fields on a block under it, each as Unity draws its type, so its numbers are number fields. It writes nothing while it draws.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ContainedEffectPacketDrawer
files.Summary: A contained effect, on one row: when it's applied, then the effect. It drew a tinted, rounded box with a stripe in its policy's color, set 50 ms after it drew.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.CrowdControlRuleDrawer
files.Summary: A crowd control rule: its tag, what it stops, and, where it stops the abilities carrying one of its tags, those tags. A stun stops every ability, so its row names none.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.CrowdControlRulesDrawer
files.Summary: A Crowd Control Rules field as a reference to an asset, with New and Open beside it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.CrowdControlRulesEditor
files.Summary: A Crowd Control Rules asset's inspector: the shared header, then its rules.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.CueHandlerDrawer
files.Summary: A cue handler, picked by its kind, as a worker is.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.CueLibraryEditor
files.Summary: A cue library's inspector: its routes, each a cue tag and the handlers it plays; then each cue tag the project's assets raise through it, by a Cue Tag cue, with the route that plays it, or that none does, and the assets that raise it, each a row that opens its asset in The Forge. It follows the project as it changes, and its routes as they're edited.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.DataWrapperDrawer
files.Summary: A Local Data row: its key, its value's kind and its value, each a column of its own, laid out by the style sheet. A value's kind is a class, Float to ScriptableObject or one of your own: a kind that holds one Value draws it in the row, and one of your own with more fields draws each under its name. Each row holds a value of its own, so a row added as a copy of the last edits its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EffectAreaDrawer
files.Summary: An effect's area's fields, drawn where it's held, as an Area component's own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EffectChangeDrawer
files.Summary: A modifier's change: its kind, always of some kind, then its fields, as a worker is drawn.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EffectModifierDrawer
files.Summary: An Effect Modifier field as a reference to an asset, with New and Open beside it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EffectModifierEditor
files.Summary: An Effect Modifier's inspector: what it's for, its rule, the effects it picks and its changes, each of a kind with its fields, and a line that says them. Unity's own fields.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EffectPurgeDrawer
files.Summary: An effect's Purges, a foldout of its fields, its arrow in line with the lists' around it in the Tags section. Unity hangs an inspector foldout's arrow 12 px into the margin, to the left of a list's arrow; this one keeps the lists' column, as pf-foldout--aligned sets in PlayForge.uss.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EffectTagRequirementsDrawer
