files.Summary: An effect's tag requirements on one side, the target's or the source's, as a table: Applying, While On and Removed By, each with what it requires and what it must not have. The drawer drew a tinted box with colored subsections, a type badge, a Name and import buttons of its own, and rebuilt itself as it opened.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EffectTemplateRegistry
files.Summary: The effects a new Cost or Cooldown effect copies, by "Cost" or "Cooldown". Project Settings → PlayForge holds them, with the project; they lived in EditorPrefs, which every project on the machine shares.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EntityDrawer
files.Summary: A reference to an entity: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EntityIdentityEditor
files.Summary: The Entity inspector: Identity, Leveling, Tags, the entity's Attributes, Abilities and Items, Workers and Local Data, then Used By. A collapsed section shows one line, and the inspector takes its look from the style sheet.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeAssetLines
files.Summary: One line for each asset, which its inspector's header and The Forge's list show: an ability's numbers by level, then its costs and cooldown, as "-450/-600/-750 Health; 280/420/680 Mana; 70/60/50 s"; an item's what it changes while equipped and the ability it grants, as "+20 Armor; Blink"; an entity's first attributes as it starts and its abilities, as "Health 500, Mana 300, Armor 5; Fireball, Blink"; an effect's first impact by level, as its Levels section reads it. Numbers that read what an editor can't give, as the target, are marked with a *.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeComponentRule<TComponent>
files.Summary: A check of one kind of component, wherever an asset holds it: an ability's, an effect's, an item's or an entity's. The validator finds it as it finds every rule, and it hears each component of its kind the asset holds, with the component's place in its list, which a problem names as its property path; an ability's inspector says its problems under the Components list. Derive from it, with a public constructor that takes nothing, for a component of your own, as PlayForge's components' rules do.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeDrawerStyles.HeaderConfig
files.Summary: Configuration for main header creation.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeDrawerStyles.HeaderResult
files.Summary: Result from CreateMainHeader containing references to update.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeDrawerStyles.SectionConfig
files.Summary: Configuration for collapsible section creation.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeDrawerStyles.SectionResult
files.Summary: Result from CreateCollapsibleSection containing references.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeDrawerStyles
files.Summary: Comprehensive UI building utilities for PlayForge editors. Provides all necessary methods to create custom editors programmatically.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeFlagsDrawer
files.Summary: A flags field of PlayForge's, which writes only what's picked. Unity's own flags field stores a value that holds every flag as Everything, -1, as it binds: an asset only looked at changed, as every effect's Purges' Applied By, Any by default; a template's child took the change as an override; and the inspector's SerializedObject moved while its bindings were still being made, which Unity asserted on (IsInSyncWithParentSerializedObject). This field shows the value without writing it, stores the flags picked of those its type has, so Everything is every flag it has now and not one it gains later, and follows an Undo.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeImportWindow.Field
files.Summary: One field the window can import, by its property path.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeImportWindow
files.Summary: The one Import window: choose a source, choose the fields that differ, each pre-checked, and import them as one Undo step. A list is replaced, unless its row asks to add to it. It serves a section's Import, a whole asset's, and a single property's, such as a worker group. A whole asset keeps its name, description, icons, asset tag, template and level link. Six windows did this before, each its own way: section import copied every field with no choice, and the Effect's Duration and Impact couldn't import.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeLint
files.Summary: What the project's assets give each other, which the content linter's checks read: the impact types its effects and impact workers deal, the gameplay events its thresholds and stop stages send, and the effects its items apply. It's gathered from every PlayForge asset, and the shared Value Pipelines and Effect Modifiers, as a check first asks, and forgotten as the validator checks the project afresh, or as an asset changes what it gives, which has every asset checked again against what's now true.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeLogSettingsBridge
files.Summary: Keeps the ForgeLog level chosen in Preferences → PlayForge and applies it to on every domain reload, since static fields reset on reload and EditorPrefs lasts.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeNewAssetWindow
files.Summary: A new asset's name and folder, then Create, as The Forge's Create menu asks. It makes the asset through the one factory a field's New uses too, : a copy of the type's New Asset default, named, with the tag its name gives, in the folder Project Settings names. The Create tab's dialog set type settings that did nothing, and logged each asset it made.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgePreset
files.Summary: A way to start a new asset: one of PlayForge's presets, which fills the new asset's fields, or one of the project's own template assets, which the new asset starts as a copy of.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgePresetMaking
files.Summary: What a preset reaches as it fills a new asset: its name, the project, and a way to make the assets it needs, each saved in its type's folder, or in the one the new asset was asked for where that isn't its type's.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgePresets
files.Summary: The presets The Forge's Create menu lists for each type: PlayForge's, then the project's templates.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeProblem
files.Summary: One problem the validator found in a PlayForge asset: the asset, how serious it is, and what's wrong.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeProblemSeverity
files.Summary: How serious a problem is: a Warning is likely a mistake, and an Error stops something working. A Note may be meant, as a trigger on an event that code sends: the Problems view lists it, and the counts and an inspector's header leave it out.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeProblemsWindow
files.Summary:
The Problems view: every problem the validator finds in the project's PlayForge assets, each with its severity and its asset, and a click selects the asset. It follows the validator, so it has no Refresh. It replaces Validate All, which showed 15 problems in a dialog nothing in could be selected, and the Audit, which wrote to the Console.

By Rule, its other view, groups the problems under the rule each breaks, and where a simple step fixes a problem, gives it a Quick Fix, and its rule a Fix All, each one Undo step.

It lists the linter's notes too, which may be meant, as a trigger on an event that code sends, under their own filter, and its counts leave them out.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeProjectEditor
files.Summary: A Forge Project's inspector: the shared header, then its settings; its catalog a line saying how many assets it names for saves and how it keeps them, where it drew each entry, a list of GUIDs as long as the project.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeQuickFix
files.Summary: A problem's quick fix: what it does, as its button says, and the step itself. The step writes through a SerializedObject, or records Undo, so the Undo step the Problems view opens around it takes it back; and the validator, which follows each edit, checks the asset again.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeRenameWindow
files.Summary: Rename, from an asset's menu in The Forge's list or its header, or F2 on The Forge's list: the asset's name, to type over, then Rename, which renames it as its inspector does (). Enter renames and Escape cancels.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeRenames
files.Summary: Renames an asset as its inspector does, from The Forge or an asset's header: a PlayForge asset's name, with the tag its name gives, as one Undo step; a Scaler asset's scaler and a Requirement template's requirements, whose names its lists show; and for an asset with no name of its own, as a Value Pipeline, its file alone. The file takes the name, with its type's prefix and suffix from Project Settings, leaving out its spaces as a new asset's file does, and follows the name back through Undo and Redo. A file that is its asset's only name keeps the spaces, and its rename Unity doesn't undo.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeSpreadsheetWindow
files.Summary: A sheet's changes before they're made: each number it changes, its asset, what it reads now and what it will, each chosen until it's unticked; what of the sheet can't be read; and Import, which makes the chosen changes as one Undo step.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeSpreadsheets
files.Summary:
Numbers by level and item stats, to and from CSV, so a game is balanced in a spreadsheet.

A sheet of numbers by level has a row for each number of an asset that reads a Table or By Level: the asset's tag and name, the field as the inspector labels it, its kind, and what it reads at each level, its values times its number, as Laguna Blade's -450/-600/-750. A sheet of item stats has a row for each item and a column for each attribute its granted effects add to: a number, or one for each level, as 10/15/20.

A sheet read back finds each row's asset by its asset tag, or by its name where it gives none; a name two assets share, an asset that isn't there and a field it hasn't got are problems, not guesses. Its changes, listed, apply as one Undo step, each number's values set so it reads what the row says.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTagLibraryEditor
files.Summary: A Tag Library's inspector: the shared header, then its entries and its contexts.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTagRegistry.ContextUsage
files.Summary: Tracks usage within a specific context.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTagRegistry.FieldUsageInfo
files.Summary: Tracks a single usage of a tag - which asset and which field path.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTagRegistry.TagContext
files.Summary: Represents a unique context where tags are used. Uses string-based context identifiers (from ForgeContext constants).

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTagRegistry.TagUsageRecord
files.Summary: Tracks usage of a single tag across contexts.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTagRegistry
files.Summary: Central registry for tracking tag usage across all PlayForge assets. Provides context-aware tag filtering and usage statistics.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTemplateConfig
files.Summary: Defines which property paths are excluded from template propagation for each asset type. Excluded fields are identity fields (name, tags, textures), linking fields (link mode, linked source), and template system internals.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTemplatePropagator
files.Summary:
Core engine for template propagation. Handles:

  • Propagating template field changes to child assets (non-overridden, non-excluded)
  • Merging list properties (additions and removals from template)
  • Detecting and recording field overrides by comparing child against template
  • Cascading propagation through template chains (A → B → C)
  • Finding all child assets of a given template via project scan

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTemplatePush
files.Summary: Templates as prefabs work. A template's changes reach its children when it's pushed to them, as an explicit step: each child, and each of theirs, takes the template's fields but those it overrides, and one Undo takes the push back. An edit to a child's field makes the field the child's own, an override, which its inspector marks, and Revert to Template takes back. Saving a template opened a dialog in the middle of the save, loaded every asset of its type, and changed the children with no Undo.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeValidationRule
files.Summary: A check the validator runs on each PlayForge asset. Derive from it, with a public constructor that takes nothing, to add a check of your own: the validator finds every one. A problem a simple step fixes can carry the step as its .

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeValidator
files.Summary: PlayForge's one validator. It runs every on each PlayForge asset in the project and keeps what they find, which the Problems view lists and an inspector's header counts. It follows the project, so nothing polls: an edit checks its asset again, an import checks what it brought, and a deleted asset has every asset checked again, since another may have read it. In batch mode, writes each problem to the Console. Validate All checked four things, flagged every effect with no workers, and showed 15 problems in a dialog.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.GameplayEffectDrawer
files.Summary: A reference to an effect: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it, and under it a line that says how the effect takes its levels, with Link to make it take them from the asset that holds the field. Its right-click menu holds the field's template, a pick of the effects nothing links, and New Linked Effect. Setting the field asked in a dialog whether to link the effect, and the template, the link filter and a create button sat beside the field as tinted buttons.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.GameplayEffectDurationDrawer
files.Summary: An effect's duration: Policy, then what the policy uses: Duration and its ticks for a Durational effect, Tick Every for an Infinite one, then Tick On Application, execute ticks, the clock, Re-application and Then, and stacking for Stack Existing. It drew its parts in tinted boxes with colored headings, under sentences that explained them, and showed or hid them 50 ms after it drew. It follows the policy as it changes, an Undo among them.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.GameplayEffectEditor
files.Summary: The Effect inspector: Identity, Leveling, Tags, Duration, Impact, Requirements, Workers and Local Data, then Used By. A collapsed section shows one line, and the inspector takes its look from the style sheet. Requirements shows the target's table, then the source's, on a two-button switch.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.GameplayEffectImpactDrawer
files.Summary: An effect's impact: the attribute, the operation, the magnitude, then how the impact is delivered, which the duration gives it, and what a periodic one commits. Then its impact types and who it affects, its additional impacts, each with a delivery of its own, with Add Impact, and its contained effects. It no longer draws Reverse On Removal, which the impact model removed, and it takes its look from the style sheet: it drew tinted boxes with colored headings.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.IForgeComponentRule
files.Summary: A rule about one kind of component, whose problems an asset's inspector shows under its Components list.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.IProxyStagePolicyDrawer
files.Summary: A proxy stage's policy: its kind, named without "ProxyStagePolicy" or "Policy", always of some kind.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.InlineFieldsDrawer
files.Summary: A field's own fields, drawn where it's held, as a component's own: a field of its whole drew a foldout inside the component.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ItemDrawer
files.Summary: A reference to an item: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ItemEditor
files.Summary: The Item inspector: Identity, Leveling, Tags, the item's Effects and Abilities, Workers and Local Data, then Used By. A collapsed section shows one line, and the inspector takes its look from the style sheet.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.LevelProviderDrawer
files.Summary: A [LinkedSource] field, the asset whose levels this one takes: Unity's object field of level providers, whose picker lists them, and under it a line of the levels it gives. It was any asset's field that warned at a wrong pick, with a tinted box, a colored type badge, a × and a "..." that opened a browser window of its own, which Unity's picker does.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.LevelThresholdDrawer
files.Summary: A Threshold scaler's threshold: the level it holds from and the tier's name on one row, Unity's fields bound to them, so an Undo shows in them, and under them what the scaler reads from there, a number field of any kind. In a list it needs no label of its own. It drew a tinted row with "Lv" in blue and an arrow as text, and its fields wrote as they changed and followed nothing after.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.MagnitudeModifierGroupMemberDrawer
files.Summary: A Scaler Group's member, cached or not, as Unity's fields: how its result combines with the members' before it, then its scaler, whose own drawer shows its kind and its settings. It drew a stripe and a symbol in the operation's color, the scaler's kind beside them, and, for a cached member, a "CACHED" badge.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.NumberFields.Walk
files.Summary: How far walks into the numbers a value holds.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.NumberFields
files.Summary: What the number field's inspector and its Problems rule know of numbers: which properties are numbers, what a field's context provides and its unit, what a kind needs and where the kind menu files it, and what a number's kind reads, inside other scalers too.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.NumberLimits
files.Summary: The limits a number field's constant keeps in the inspector, from its , and , in what the field stores.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.NumberSiblingFieldDrawer
files.Summary: The field a relative number reads, picked from a menu of the other number fields of the object that holds the number, each by its name as the inspector writes it. The number's own field and any field that reads it back stay out, so a loop can't be picked. A name the object no longer has, as after a rename, shows as missing.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.PlayForgeGASProfilerModule
files.Summary: The PlayForge GAS module in Unity's Profiler: the GAS's counters, charted: its entities by hub, its effects, impacts, activations and refusals, and its tag compiles and recomputes.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.PlayForgePreferences
files.Summary: PlayForge's view toggles, which belong to each user rather than to the project, so they stay in EditorPrefs, as Unity's own preferences do, and the Preferences page edits them. The settings the project shares are .

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.PlayForgeProcessesProfilerModule
files.Summary: The PlayForge Processes module in Unity's Profiler: ProcessControl's and TaskSequence's counters, charted, and in its details the selected frame's costliest processes, which PlayForge puts into the capture as the frame's metadata while the Profiler records.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.PlayForgeSettings
files.Summary: PlayForge's authoring settings, a Forge Project's, so they travel with the project under version control: where each type's new assets go, the defaults a new asset copies and Import lists first, and the effects a new Cost or Cooldown copies. A new asset's file is its name alone. The Project Settings page edits them; the view toggles stay in Preferences (). The file and the EditorPrefs a project took them from once are gone with that taking.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ProcessInstantiatorDrawer
files.Summary: A process's instantiator: its kind, or None, then its fields.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.PurgeFilterDrawer
files.Summary: A purge's filter: its kind, named without "Purge Filter", as Except Tagged, or one of your own, then the kind's own fields.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.QuickFillWizard.EFillPattern
files.Summary: The shape the values take from the first to the last.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.QuickFillWizard.ERounding
files.Summary: How the values are rounded once made.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.QuickFillWizard
files.Summary: Quick Fill, from a scaler field's menu: what it fills, the scaler's levels or its points; a pattern and its values; rounding; and a preview of the values as the scaler's table shows them, with their curve, and, for a scaler spread over levels, what each level reads between its points. Apply writes them, and the curve a spread scaler reads, as one Undo step. It drew a look of its own, a purple bold title, a green Apply, 10 px hints and tinted boxes, from styles set in C#, with its fields outside the label column, and wrote through a property it kept from when it opened.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.RequirementTemplateEditor
files.Summary: A Requirement Template's inspector: the shared header, then its fields.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.RespawnPlaceDrawer
files.Summary: A Respawn's place: its kind, Home, Where It Died or Point, or one of your own, named without "Respawn Place", then the kind's own fields, as Point's point.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.RuntimeDebugger
files.Summary: The Debugger: one window for the game as it plays, in place of the GAS Debugger, Process Control and the Tag Debugger. Its Entities view lists the hubs ProcessControl registers, of either kind, beside one hub's attributes, effects, abilities and tags, which it can change. Its Processes view lists every process, with what it's doing and how long its steps take, and its Tags view every tag the entities hold, as a tree, beside who holds the one selected. Its Timeline view shows what the entities' abilities and effects did over time, as a recorder heard it. The lists follow ProcessControl as processes join and leave, and the values change in place, at the rate the window menu sets, while the game plays. Outside Play mode it offers Play Mode. The GAS Debugger scanned the scene for MonoBehaviour hubs and rebuilt its details every 0.25 s; Process Control and the Tag Debugger were IMGUI windows of their own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.SaveScalerAssetWindow
files.Summary: Save as Scaler Asset, from a magnitude field's menu: a name and a folder, then Save and Use, which saves the field's scaler as a Scaler asset and makes the field share it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ScalableFloatDrawer
files.Summary: A number field: its name, then its kind, Constant or another, and either its number or its range, as in "6–8 s", and its field menu. Another kind adds a one-line summary of what it reads, how the field combines its number with the kind, then the kind's own content: its values per level and their curve, its Scaler asset, or its fields. The kind menu files kinds by category and offers only those the field's context resolves (), and a field whose unit is "%" shows and takes its number as a percentage. Its constant keeps the field's limits, on a slider where it has a range, and its label shows the field's tooltip.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ScalableIntDrawer
files.Summary: A whole-number field, such as Ticks: the same field, with its rounding.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ScalerActions
files.Summary: What a magnitude field's kind menu and field menu do, each as one Undo step that reaches every selected asset. Each asset's field changes from its own values, through a SerializedObject of its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ScalerAssetEditor
files.Summary: A Scaler asset's inspector: its name, kind and how many fields use it, its Description, its values, and the fields that use it, each a row that selects its asset. Its Name names it, as menus and The Forge list it; it could only be read, so a Scaler asset couldn't be renamed in The Forge.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ScalerBehaviourDrawer
files.Summary: A scaler's behaviour: its kind, named without "ScalerBehaviour" or "Behaviour", then the kind's own fields. The picker offers no None: a list's "−" removes a behaviour. An empty slot stays empty as it's drawn.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ScalerDrawer
files.Summary: A scaler field drawn on its own, such as an effect's Delta Time Scaler or an attribute set element's Scaling: its name and kind, the range it gives, then its content: its values per level with their curve, Stretch Over Levels, the kind's own fields and its behaviours, or a Shared scaler's asset. It drew a tinted box with a colored border, a collapse arrow, Quick Fill tabs and an import button, and rebuilt itself on a copy of the first selected asset, so an edit after a rebuild reached that asset alone. It writes nothing while it draws. Its kinds file by category, as a number field's do, and its field menu is a number field's: Save as Scaler Asset, the Scaler assets, Import Values, Quick Fill and Make Constant.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ScalerTry.AttributeRow
files.Summary: An attribute a side holds for a read: whether it has it, and its current and base values.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ScalerTry.CallerRow
files.Summary: A key a caller sets for a read, with its value, or not set.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ScalerTry.Reading
files.Summary: What a read gave: its levels, the value at each, and the parts behind each.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ScalerTry.Side
files.Summary: The caster or the target: the attributes the read asked of it, and the entity they were filled from.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ScalerTry
files.Summary:
A scaler tried in the editor: read at each level of a range against stand-ins for its caster and its target, which hold the values typed for them or filled from an entity's attribute set, and with the values a caller sets. A read finds what the scaler asks for, each attribute on its side and each caller's key, and adds a row for each the first time, filled from its side's entity where it has one. A row it lacks reads as an entity without the attribute does, and a caller's key not set reads as a caller that didn't set it.

A stand-in holds attributes alone: a number that reads an effect on a side, an item, a tag, a retention group's part or Local Data reads as it would on an entity with none of them. A Scaler asset's try, from , is kept for the session with , and never written into the asset.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ScalerValuesWindow
files.Summary: Import Values, from a magnitude field's menu: choose a Scaler asset or another asset's field, compare their values level by level, with both curves, and Copy Values into the field as one Undo step. A shorter table's last value holds for the levels past its end. It replaces the scaler import window, which ignored the kinds a field allows and kept its list for 120 s.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.SectionClearUtility
files.Summary: Clears a section's properties to a new asset's values, and empties its lists. Each field took its type's default, 0 or the first choice, so a cleared Impact allowed no target and had no chance to apply.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.SequenceInjectionDrawer
files.Summary: An Inject task's injection: its kind, named without "Injection", always of some kind.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.SpreadsheetChange
files.Summary: One change a sheet makes: a number of an asset, what it reads now, and what it will.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.SpreadsheetImport
files.Summary: What a sheet would change in the project's assets, and what of it can't be read.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.StackBehaviourDrawer
files.Summary: A stack behaviour, as an effect's Stack Behaviours list holds it: its kind, picked from the behaviours there are, then its fields, folding to a line of their values, as a worker is drawn. The behaviours configure a stacking container, a type apart from the one the effect behaviour drawer takes, so they had no drawer: Unity's own field gave a new element no kind to pick, and none could be added. Each is named for what it does.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.StandardWorkerGroupDrawer
files.Summary:
A worker group: its four lists of workers, each Unity's reorderable list, where a new worker starts empty for its kind to be picked. The Workers section it's drawn in folds, counts and imports it. Its name, which nothing reads, it doesn't draw.

It was a box of its own, with a colored border, colored count badges, a type tag and an Import of its own, from 90 styles set in C#, inside a section whose header already counted and imported it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.StartingItemDrawer
files.Summary: A starting item on one row: the item, then an Equip checkbox, which equips it as it's given. It drew as a foldout holding Item and Equip On Init.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.TagDrawer
files.Summary: A tag field: Unity's field, its label in the label column, the tag's parents in secondary text and its leaf in strong text, by its display name (). Pressing it opens the tag picker, Unity's searchable dropdown of the tags its context offers (), with None and, where the field may make one, New Tag… (). Its right-click menu clears it, makes a new tag, makes its tag a child of another, or copies its path. It was a button with a colored left border, a 120 px label it dropped for any field inside a list, text that changed as the pointer passed, and a picker drawn under it in tinted boxes in code, with a button that showed only on hover.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.TagQueryDrawer
files.Summary: A tag query, in Unity's aligned fields: its tag, which tags match it, then how many it counts, as its comparison and its number on one row, "Count Greater Than 0" for has the tag. It drew a tinted box with labels of its own size and color.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.TargetingTaskDrawer
files.Summary: An ability's targeting task: its kind, named without "TargetTask" or "Task", then its fields.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.TaskSequenceReferenceDrawer
files.Summary:
A sequence reference: a field as a kind field is, the sequence's name in its box, which opens a searchable dropdown of the project's sequences, the static methods marked [TaskSequenceMethod] that take nothing and return a sequence, by their names, None first, each class's under its name where more than one class holds them. A pick is one Undo step. A method the reference names that the project no longer has shows as missing until another is picked.

It was Unity's popup, one long list, and before that an IMGUI popup, which wrote "(None)", and which searched every type of every assembly for the methods.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.TheForge
files.Summary: The Forge, PlayForge's main window: a list of the project's PlayForge assets beside a detail pane that holds the selected asset's inspector, under a summary of what it does and what uses it. The toolbar holds Create, the type filters, Tags, the search and the problem count; the status bar holds the counts. It follows the project, with no Refresh and no timer, and the validator's problems with it. One click selects a row and shows its asset. It had Create, View, Analysis and Settings tabs: the Analysis tab's power scores stay hidden until Items and Entities score too, and the Settings tab's settings are on the two settings pages.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.TypePickerCache
files.Summary: The concrete classes a type allows, by name, kept per type for the editor session; a kind field's picker lists them. Its own picker window, the field that opened it and the TypeRef it wrote went unused, and went.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ValuePipelineDrawer
files.Summary: A Value Pipeline field as a reference to an asset: New beside it while it's empty, which makes one where The Forge makes assets and uses it, and Open once it names one. It was Unity's bare object field.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ValuePipelineEditor
files.Summary: A Value Pipeline's inspector: what it's for, its stages in order, each of a kind with its fields, and a line that says them; then its Try section, a value put through its stages at each level, as a Scaler asset's Try reads its scaler. Unity's own fields.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ValuePipelineTry.Reading
files.Summary: What a read gave: the value it put in, its levels, and the run at each.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ValuePipelineTry.Run
files.Summary: A level's run: each stage's step and what came out, or the stop that stopped the hit.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ValuePipelineTry
files.Summary:
A Value Pipeline tried in the editor: a value put through its stages at each level of a range, against the stand-ins a Scaler asset's try reads against, a caster's and a target's attributes, typed or filled from an entity, and the values a caller sets. Each chance a stage rolls comes up where it can, or misses where it can, as says, so a read gives the same each time. A Block or Evade stage rolls first, as it does as an effect lands, and one that comes up stops the hit before the pipeline runs: nothing of it lands.

No effect is behind a try, so a stage that reads the hit's carrier reads none, and what an Absorb stage soaks comes off no one. A pipeline's try, from , is kept for the session with , and never written into the asset.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ValueStageDrawer
files.Summary: A pipeline stage: its kind, always of some kind, then its fields, as a worker is drawn.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.VarianceDrawer
files.Summary: A Randomized scaler's variance: its kind, Percentage, Flat or Multiplier, or one of your own, named without "Variance", then the kind's own numbers, as Multiplier's Min and Max.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectArea
files.Summary: An effect's area: as the effect lands on its target, it lands on each the area takes near that target too, as Storm Hammer stuns everyone near the one it hits. Each is found by its position, on either hub, with no collider needed; an effect that lands by an area spreads no further.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectChanges
files.Summary: What modifiers changed of one application: the effect's own reads take these in, its contained effects, its impacts' numbers, its overflow, its time, its stacks, its chance and its granted tags. Null on a spec no modifier changed, so an effect nothing modifies costs nothing more.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectComponentContext
files.Summary: What an effect's component hears a moment of its effect with.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectConditions
files.Summary: An effect's conditions, beside the tags of each phase of its requirements: those that must hold for it to land, those that keep it going, and those that take it off, as Attribute Shift stops at its floor. A phase passes only when its tags pass and its conditions all hold; the Ongoing and Removal ones are checked at each frame's end while it lasts, as no tag needs to change for an attribute a condition reads to.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectJournal
files.Summary: An effect journal: each application, refusal (by requirement, immunity or chance), tick, impact and removal of an effect on the entities it listens to, with its number's trace as it lands, and each worker that ran for it, by its hook and its side, with the actions it queued and whether they ran. It keeps its last entries, oldest first. It records only while it listens, and an entity no journal listens to pays nothing: the Creator Lab's bottom panel and the Debugger's Timeline read one.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectJournalAction
files.Summary: An action a worker queued, as a journal keeps it: what it said it was, and whether it ran.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectJournalEntry
files.Summary: One entry of an effect journal: when, of what kind, on whom, the effect and who applied it, and what the kind says: why it was refused, how many ticks, the change it made, or which worker ran, at which of its effect's moments, on whose side, with the actions it queued.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectLevelSeries
files.Summary: One effect evaluated across a level range: duration, ticks, and impacts.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectModifier
files.Summary: A modifier shared between assets: a rule that an item's, an ability's, an effect's or an entity's modifier entry names in place of its own, as a Value Pipeline is shared. Its class has a file of its own name, which an asset needs to find its script: in EffectModifiers.cs, an Effect Modifier saved as an asset came back with no script, and a search by its type found none.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectModifierEntry
files.Summary: A modifier an item, an ability, an effect or an entity holds: its own rule, or a shared Effect Modifier's, which it names in place of its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectModifierRule
files.Summary: What a modifier changes, and of which effects: the effects it picks, by tag, its direction and a condition, and its changes to each effect as it's made, which last as long as that application does.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectModifierSet
files.Summary: The modifiers an entity holds now: its own, its items' while they're equipped, its abilities' while it knows them, and its effects' while they last. Each holds as often as it's given, as two of an item modify twice.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectModifiers
files.Summary: Gives a holder the modifiers it has, takes them back, and applies them to each effect as it's made.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectPurge
files.Summary: A purge: its strength, a tier of the project's purge levels, taking the effects at that tier or under it; only those of the kinds it names, by their tags, as Status.Debuff; only those applied by whom it says, against the one purged; and only those its filters take.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectSave
files.Summary: An effect on the entity's shelf, with what applied it and its clock: its stacks, its duration and period, and each stack's time left and to its next tick. A clock has one of each, unless its stacks have their own durations.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectScopedAction
files.Summary: Base class for actions scoped to an effect's lifecycle. Automatically invalidates if the effect is removed.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectStacksScaler
files.Summary: The stack count of the effect's own container: 1 for an effect that doesn't stack. With Multiply With Scaler, a stacking effect's change grows by the stack, as a sunder of −5 armor a stack does, and a Continuous change reads the count again as it changes. Only a scaler written for it read an effect's stack count.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectSystemComponent
files.Summary:
The effect shelf — apply / tick / re-apply / remove for gameplay effects, shared by BOTH and the MonoBehaviour (the twin-drift class of bugs ends here; the GAS classes keep only thin delegating wrappers).

Lifecycle under the two-kind impact model:

Apply (durational):  shelve container
                     → RegisterModifier per Continuous entry
                     → app workers
                     → commit OnApply entries; TickOnApplication? then Periodic ones once
Tick:                commit Periodic entries per execute tick
Remove:              container.OnRemove() → UnregisterModifier per Continuous entry.
                     Commits are permanent — there is no rollback path.
Instant:             commit OnApply entries — no shelf, no removal phase.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectTagRequirements
files.Summary: Tag requirements for effect application, ongoing, and removal phases. Each phase can have its own set of required and avoided tags.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectWorkerContext
files.Summary: Context for effect workers.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EffectWorkerRun
files.Summary: An effect's worker hearing one of its effect's moments, as the entity it ran on tells it. Told only where something listens, so a worker no one hears costs nothing more.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EntityClock
files.Summary: An entity's own time: the game's, as reads it, scaled by the entity's : the scale code sets, as a hit-stop's, times the one its Time Scale attribute gives, as a slow's or a haste's, so the two compose. The entity's effects tick by it, its cooldowns among them, and so do its abilities' sequences and waits. Every entity ran on Unity's one clock, so nothing could slow one entity and not the rest. A scale of 0 holds the entity's time still; it isn't a pause, which ProcessControl's is, and processes keep their own bookkeeping on the game's clock. It's a clock as any other is, so a sequence that isn't an ability's runs on an entity's time with its packet's set to it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EntityComponentContext
files.Summary: What an entity's component hears a moment of its entity with.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EntityDeath
files.Summary: What an entity does as it dies and as it revives: a MOBA hero, or anyone who dies and comes back, keeps its entity while its body goes. Where it stays: the effects its death ends, by tag, as buffs; the effects it takes as it dies, as a respawn timer; the effects it takes as it revives, as its health back; and its body, a MonoBehaviour process it spawns where it is, as it starts and as it revives, and ends as it dies. A runtime entity takes its position from its body.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EvadeStage
files.Summary: An evade: on its chance, nothing of the effect lands, as a dodge.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ExceptTaggedPurgeFilter
files.Summary: Spares the effects carrying one of its tags, as their asset tag or a context tag, as a purge that leaves stuns.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ExecuteStage
files.Summary: An execute: a hit that would leave the one hit with less than a share of its attribute's base takes the rest, as Culling Blade does below its threshold.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.FacingValidation
files.Summary: Facing: the target lies within an angle in front of its caster, or the caster within an angle behind its target, as a backstab wants; each facing its targeting packet's, along the ground. An angle of 360 takes anywhere.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.FlatVariance
files.Summary: Up or down by an amount, as 5 for a hit of 20 landing from 15 to 25.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.FloatingTextCue
files.Summary: Floats a text where its placement says, above the one the cue is on by default: a hit's damage from an effect's On Hit, the gold a kill gave, a status's name as it lands. It says its Text, where {value} is its number, written as its Value says, {name} the name of what raised it, as an effect's, and {tag} its cue tag; it moves, fades and scales as its Motion says, looks as its Look says, and merges, staggers and caps as its Stacking says. Its texts come from and go back to it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.FloatingTextLook
files.Summary: How a floating text looks.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.FloatingTextMotion
files.Summary: How a floating text moves and fades over its life.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.FloatingTextStacking
files.Summary: How the floating texts on one entity merge, stagger, and how many show.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.FloatingTextValue
files.Summary: A floating text's number, and how it's written.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeAssetCatalog
files.Summary:
Names the assets a save refers to, attributes, effects, abilities and items, by IDs that last across sessions, as a reference doesn't. A save names each by its ID here, and a load finds it by that.

In the editor, Add Every PlayForge Asset, in the catalog's menu, names each PlayForge asset in the project by its GUID, which lasts as the asset is renamed or moved. A game can add its own as it runs.

A is the catalog the Create menu makes, of the assets in its folder, which it keeps current as they're made, moved in and deleted; a catalog made before goes on naming what it names.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeAuras
files.Summary: Gives a holder an aura, and takes it back: what each Aura component does in its own hooks, and a game's code may do for an aura of its own. An entity's auras are its , a service it steps.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeAuthoringSettings
files.Summary: How The Forge makes a Forge Project's assets: where each type's new assets go, each type's defaults, and the effects a new Cost or Cooldown copies. They were the whole Unity project's, in ProjectSettings/PlayForgeSettings.asset; each game keeps its own now. A game's build ignores them.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeChance
files.Summary: Every chance PlayForge rolls goes through here: a number of the chance, the caster's luck, and, where the chance is pseudo-random, the caster's streak for it, kept by the chance's key.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeCombatLog
files.Summary: The current project's combat log settings, which each entity's log reads as it writes.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeContext
files.Summary:
The contexts a tag is offered in: one per kind of tag, what a tag is rather than where it's used. A tag field names the kinds it takes with [ForgeTagContext], and its picker offers the tags of those kinds: those assets use in such a field, those a Tag Library declares for them, and those code exposes with [ForgeTagExposed].

Usage: [ForgeTagContext(ForgeContext.Granted)] public Tag Stunned;

Each constant is its value without its spaces. A project's own contexts, made in a contexts field's New Context…, stand beside these.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeCounters
files.Summary: PlayForge's counters in Unity's Profiler, in its PlayForge category, which the PlayForge Processes and PlayForge GAS modules chart. A frame's counts start from 0 each frame, and count every world's work, a headless run's within the frame among them. A level holds until it changes: the scene's ProcessControl gives the process levels as its LateUpdate loop ends, and the others follow what starts and ends. Unity compiles them out of release builds, so they count in the editor and development builds. A ProfilerRecorder reads one by its name in the category, as "Effects Applied". The markers time PlayForge's work; these say how much of it there is.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeCuePool
files.Summary: The pools pooled Prefab cues take their objects from: one per prefab, its idle objects put away under a root that outlives a scene, in place of an object made and destroyed each time a cue plays.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeCueRoutes
files.Summary: Plays a cue by its tag, as a Cue Tag cue raises it: the entity's own Cue Receiver first, its own way; then, where the receiver plays nothing for it or passes it through, the library's route for the tag, the receiver's variant's where the library has one.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeCueSink
files.Summary: What a world asks once for each raise of a list of cues, before any of them plays: whether it plays here. The default plays everything; a network layer's says what a server plays, what it sends on, and what a client has played ahead. Give a world one of its own with .

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeCues
files.Summary: Where every cue plays, whatever raised it: an effect's, an ability's, an entity's, an item's, or a game's own code, as sparks at a ray's hit. A handler that throws is reported and the rest play on: what something shows mustn't stop what it does. And what PlayForge's cues reach in the game: the camera shaker the game gives.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeEffectTemplateAttribute
files.Summary: Marks a GameplayEffect field as template-able. The drawer will show an "Import from Template" option when a template is configured.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeEntities
files.Summary: Every live entity, on both hubs: each joins as its core initializes and leaves as it ends. An area search goes through it, as Auto Target and Auto Target by Affinity do: with no range they searched the scene for MonoBehaviour entities alone, so a runtime entity was never found; and with a range they searched with physics alone, which finds no runtime entity, as it has no collider.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeEvents
files.Summary: Sends a gameplay event to an entity as the core sends its own: only where an ability of the entity listens for it, queued for its frame's end where it has a queue, its data the source and the subject given.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeFloatingText
files.Summary: A text a Floating Text cue floats: it moves, fades and scales over its life by its cue's motion, on the game's clock or in real time, faces the camera where asked, and goes back to its pool as its life ends. A number merged into it starts its life again.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeFrameCosts
files.Summary: A frame's costliest processes, which go into the Profiler's capture as the frame's metadata while the Profiler records, for the PlayForge Processes module to list. The costs go under , the costliest first, and each one's type's name, in UTF-8, under the tags after it in the same order, so a saved capture still names them. The scene's ProcessControl puts them in as its frame ends; while the Profiler doesn't record, nothing is timed for them.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeInput
files.Summary: The input click targeting reads: the project's own, unless puts another in. Targeting read the Input Manager's mouse and Camera.main itself, so a game on the Input System, with a camera of its own or a test couldn't stand in, and a scene with no main camera threw at the click. A source-scanning test keeps Unity's input out of the rest of the runtime.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeLifesteal
files.Summary: Lifesteal's one rule, an effect's and a holder's.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeLog.ESystem
files.Summary: The part of PlayForge a message is of, each able to take a level of its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeLog
files.Summary:
Level-gated logging for PlayForge: all the runtime says goes through here, and this file alone writes to Unity's console, so a project sets how much it hears in one place: Preferences → PlayForge → Logging in the editor, kept and put back on a domain reload, or from code.

Each message is of a system, effects, abilities, workers, numbers, processes, sequences and the rest, and a system can take a level of its own, , as the Creator Lab's log does; hears each message let through, with the entity it's about where it names one.

What's said only when asked, a debug tool's output (TagCache.LogWeights, the Threshold Debugger worker, LogAction), ProcessControl's logs while its inspector's toggles are on, and a sequence's injection or chain logging, is information: the toggle decides whether it's made, and the level whether it's shown.

Its methods are marked to hide in the Console's stack, as the Console's Strip Logging Callstack hides them, and a double-click on a message it wrote opens the code that logged it, not this file.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeLogEntry
files.Summary: One message ForgeLog let through: its level, its system, the message, and whom it's about.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeMenuAttribute
files.Summary:
Files a kind in the pickers that offer it, an ability task's, a worker's, a component's, a cue's, a number's and the rest: under the submenus its path names, a slash between each, as "Effects" or "Effects/Damage"; with a name to show in place of its class's; and with a description the picker's Context says while it's highlighted.

A path holds for the classes made from the one that names it, unless one names its own, "" for the picker's top; a kind that names only a name or a description keeps its base's path. A name and a description are a kind's own. A picker lists a menu's submenus in name order, then its kinds; its search finds a kind whatever its submenu.

It replaces ForgeCategory, the ability tasks' one level of groups, and the Category of a number's kind and of a condition, each of which filed one family alone. 

[Serializable]
[ForgeMenu("Effects/Damage", Description = "Deals its damage to each target, once")]
public class StrikeTask : AbstractAbilityTask { ... }

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeProcessCost
files.Summary: One of a frame's costliest processes in the Profiler's capture: its process ID, and the time its steps took in the frame, every timing's.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeProfiler
files.Summary: PlayForge's markers in Unity's Profiler, so what it runs shows there by its own name: the step loop at each timing, a process's step, under one of its type's too, a GAS's step and its end of frame, an effect's application, an ability's activation, a tag compile, an attribute's recompute and a stage's start. Runtime had none, so PlayForge's cost showed only as its callers'. Each is a sample in the Scripts category, which a ProfilerRecorder can read by its name, as "PlayForge.ApplyEffect".

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeProject
files.Summary: A Forge Project: a set of PlayForge assets of its own, those under the folder its asset is in. The Forge shows the active project's assets alone, and makes new assets in it. A project's folder can hold another project's, and an asset is in the innermost project whose folder holds it. It's an asset catalog too, of its own assets, for saves, which it keeps current as they're made, moved in and deleted; Add Its Assets names them by hand.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeProjectSettings
files.Summary: A Forge Project's settings: what its game reads as it runs, its attributes' roles and the crowd control rules an entity follows where it names none of its own. A running game finds them through its GameRoot.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgePurge
files.Summary: What purges an entity's effects: those a purge takes, by the current project's purge levels, each coming off as a removal does.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeRandom
files.Summary: The random numbers PlayForge's runtime draws: Unity's, unless puts another source in, as . The runtime drew from UnityEngine.Random in five files, so a roll could be repeated only by seeding the whole game's random numbers.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeReach
files.Summary: What reads an ability's reach, its first component's: how far it reaches, and whether a target or a point lies beyond it, from its caster. An ability with none reaches anywhere. Each read that takes a reach reads that one, as a component of more than one reach asks its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeResolveOrder
files.Summary: The project's resolve order: the order an area's effects land on those it takes, by the tags they carry, so specific behaviour can be coded. An ability's Apply Effects and Apply/Remove Effects, an effect's Area, with its target among those it takes, and an aura's check follow it; code of your own can too.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeRoles
files.Summary: The attributes playing roles in the current project: PlayForge's features read the roles it ships, as , and a game's code reads its own by their tags.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeSave
files.Summary:
Saves an entity at rest and loads it back. Nothing captured an entity's state, so a game couldn't keep a battle between sessions.

takes what lasts on an entity into a : its attributes' permanent commits, its levels, the abilities it knows, its items with their stacks, worn or not, its effects with their time left, its loose tags and its time scale. Modifiers aren't saved: they come back with the effects that carry them. ends what's running, lets go of what the entity has, and puts back what the save had, on the entity it was taken from or a fresh one of its kind.

A restore tells nothing as it goes. No effect is told as applied or removed, no attribute as changed, and nothing of an effect's application runs again: its workers, its commits on application, its contained effects. It tells once, as it ends, for a listener to read the entity afresh.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeShowWhenAttribute
files.Summary: Shows a field in its inspector only while another field of the same object holds one of the values given, as a randomized scaler's multipliers show only for its Multiplier mode. The inspector reads it; nothing at runtime does. The other field is an enum or a bool. A field can carry several, and shows while every one holds, as an Asset Part number's worker key shows only for an effect's Worker Value.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeSnapshot
files.Summary: An entity at rest, as takes it and puts it back: its attributes' permanent commits, its levels, abilities, items and effects, its loose tags and its time scale. Plain serializable types, so a game writes a save where it likes, through JsonUtility or its own serializer. Assets are named by their IDs in a and tags by name, which last across sessions as a reference doesn't.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTagContext
files.Summary:
The kinds of tag a tag field takes, which its picker offers: one context per kind, as ForgeContext names them, or a project's own.

Usage: [ForgeTagContext(ForgeContext.Granted, ForgeContext.AssetTag)] public Tag Required;

Or with string literals: [ForgeTagContext("Granted", "Asset Tag")] public Tag Required;

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTagDefault
files.Summary: Specifies a default tag value for a field if none is set.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTagExcludeUniversal
files.Summary: Controls whether Universal tags are included when filtering by context. By default, Universal tags are always included.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTagExposed
files.Summary: Exposes a tag written in code to the editor's tag pickers, on a static Tag property or field, a project's own as PlayForge's in Tags: only a code tag marked so is offered, so a project chooses which of its tags its designers see. Its contexts say which fields offer it; with none, it's under Code. It was ForgeContextDefault, which a property alone could carry.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTagGroup
files.Summary: Groups related tag fields together in the inspector.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTagLibrary
files.Summary:
A project-authored tag catalogue: tags that exist by declaration rather than by being referenced somewhere in an asset. The Forge's Create tab writes entries here, and the editor tag registry (ForgeTagRegistry) scans every library asset so declared tags appear in tag pickers under their chosen contexts — even before any asset uses them.

Multiple libraries may exist (e.g. one per feature); all are scanned.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTagLockedCountAttribute
files.Summary: Attribute to mark a Tag list field as having locked items determined by count. Tags at indices less than LockedCount are locked.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTagLockedIndicesAttribute
files.Summary: Attribute to mark specific indices in a Tag list as locked.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTagNoCreate
files.Summary: Prevents creating new tags from this field's dropdown.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTagPrefix
files.Summary: Specifies that this tag field should only accept tags matching specific prefixes.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTagReadOnly
files.Summary: Marks a tag field as read-only in the inspector. The tag can still be set programmatically.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTagRequired
files.Summary: Validates that a tag field is not empty when the asset is saved.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTagTooltip
files.Summary: Provides a custom tooltip for the tag field.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTick
files.Summary: The fixed-rate tick. With ProcessControl's tick rate set, the game steps in ticks, each a fixed step of its time, a number of them a frame: every process steps once a tick, its end of frame with it, and a sequence waits for the next tick where it waited for the next frame. So a run comes out the same at any frame rate. Off, as it is by default, a wait is Unity's next frame, as it was. A world of its own has a tick of its own, in force while it steps or moves a process, so its sequences wait on its steps. The ticks run on the game's time and stand with it, so a sequence on a clock that runs while it stands, as does, waits for Unity's frames.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTickSource
files.Summary: A tick: the waits for its next one, which it lets go as it ticks, and how many it has run. The scene has one, which ProcessControl's tick rate turns on, and each world of its own has its own, which ticks as its owner steps it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTime
files.Summary: The clock PlayForge's runtime reads: Unity's, unless puts another in. The runtime read Unity's Time in a dozen files, so nothing could step it to a clock of its own, as a deterministic replay, a server or a test needs. A source-scanning test keeps Time out of the runtime.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTurnToFace
files.Summary: What turns an activation's caster to face its target or its point before its first stage, as an entity's Turns To Face and an ability's Turn To Face do.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeWorkerNames
files.Summary: A worker's kind in a word or two, as a journal or a log names it: "Math" for a MathAttributeWorker.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.FrameSummary
files.Summary:
Captures all modifications and events that occurred during a frame for a single GAS.

Impact tracking is split by perspective: • Impact RECEIVED — indexed by ISource (who attacked me) • Impact DEALT — indexed by ITarget (who I attacked)

A self-impact (source == target on the same system) is recorded on both sides.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.FrameSummarySnapshot
files.Summary: A frame's summary as its listeners read it. The one hands a listener is its entity's own and is refilled each frame, so it holds that frame only during the call. makes one to keep.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameClock
files.Summary: The game's time, as the clock in force reads it: ForgeTime's own, or a world's or a tick's while one steps. It reads that clock each time it's asked, so it can be kept and handed on: a sequence on it runs by the game's time whatever its packet's owner's is, as an ability's caster's.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameClockChoice
files.Summary: The game's time, whatever an ability's caster's is: a slowed caster's sequence on it isn't slowed.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameRoot
files.Summary: The game's own entity, a Mono hub every scene has one of, which ProcessControl hands any registration that names no handler. It runs as its Forge Project's Game Root entity: the project a scene's Bootstrapper plays, or else its own, or else the entity it names. It keeps through scene loads.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameplayAbilitySystem
files.Summary: A GAS on a GameObject. What makes it a GAS lives in , which it builds as it initializes and forwards to. What stays here is the asset it is made from, its place in the scene, and how it goes away.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.ActionFailedDelegate
files.Summary: Invoked when an action fails as its turn comes: its IsValid or its Execute threw. It's written to the Console too, and the rest of the queue runs on.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.ActionQueuedDelegate
files.Summary: Invoked when an action is queued for deferred execution. An action the system makes for itself, such as a rescale or a lifesteal's heal, is used again once the queue has run it, so read it during the call.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.ChangeStepDelegate
files.Summary: A step a change to one of this entity's attributes took, as it was taken: an attribute worker's, a barrier's soak or a gain's scaling.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.EffectDelegate
files.Summary: Invoked when an effect is applied.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.EffectRefusedDelegate
files.Summary: An effect that didn't land on this entity, and why.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.EffectTickDelegate
files.Summary: Invoked when an effect ticks.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.EffectWorkerDelegate
files.Summary: An effect's worker heard one of its effect's moments on this entity: its own, or a hit it dealt.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.FrameCompleteDelegate
files.Summary: Invoked at the end of each frame after all deferred actions are processed. Provides a complete summary of all modifications that occurred. The summary is the entity's own and is refilled each frame, so read it during the call, or copy what you need.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.ImpactWorkerDelegate
files.Summary: One of this entity's impact workers ran for a hit it dealt.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.SystemDelegate
files.Summary: Invoked when the system is initialized.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.TagWorkerDelegate
files.Summary: Invoked when a tag worker is activated.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks
files.Summary: Callbacks for the GameplayAbilitySystem level events. These are frame-level and cross-system events, distinct from AbilitySystemCallbacks (ability events) and AttributeSystemCallbacks (attribute events).

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameplayCondition
files.Summary:
A condition read against a number's context: whether something holds where the number is read, as "the target's Health is below 0.3 of its base". A Conditional scaler reads one to choose its branch. It is a class, so a project adds its own as it adds a kind of number: override , and name it, file it and say what it reads with :

[Serializable]
[GameplayCondition("Target Is Caster", Reads = NumberReads.Caster | NumberReads.Target)]
public class TargetIsCaster : GameplayCondition
{
    protected override bool Evaluate(in NumberContext context) => ReferenceEquals(context.Caster, context.Target);

    public override string Describe() => "the target is the caster";
}

Where the context lacks what a condition reads, as a target's tag where there's no target, it doesn't hold, and it logs once. A condition's own numbers read with the condition as their owner. Its fields draw in the inspector with no editor code, with [Tooltip] and [ForgeShowWhen]; it is saved by its class's name, as a [SerializeReference] value is, so renaming the class needs Unity's [MovedFrom].

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameplayConditionAttribute
files.Summary: Names a condition in the condition menu and says what it reads of a number's context. Its place in the menu is its 's: it named a Category of its own. Without it, a condition takes its class's name without "Condition", and is read everywhere.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GrantTagsChange
files.Summary: Adds tags it grants while it's on, as its own granted tags are.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GrantTagsTask
files.Summary: Grants tags to its caster or its target while its stage runs, as a charge's State.Charging: on as it starts, off as the stage ends, however it ends. Each is a loose tag, counted as a grant is, so two runs at once each give and take back their own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GroupContribution
files.Summary: One group's slice of an attribute's ActiveValue (see ).

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GroupImpactKind
files.Summary: One retention group's part of an attribute, on the caster or the target, current or base: an attribute's value is the sum of its groups' parts, so 2 × Caster's Strength (Bonus) deals more for the Strength items give and nothing for the hero's own. An entity with no such attribute, or no part in the group, reads 0.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.GroupProcess
files.Summary:
A container process that other processes can register into.

Members are still their own processes in ProcessControl — they move through Running/Waiting/Terminated as normal. The group adds coordinated lifecycle management, shared data, member-cap enforcement, and group-level operations.

Usage: // Registration auto-creates the group if it doesn't exist: ProcessControl.RegisterWithGroup(myGroupTag, someProcess, out relay);

// Or create the group manually for configuration: var group = new GroupProcess("Buffs", maxMembers: 5, overflowPolicy: EGroupOverflowPolicy.EvictOldest); ProcessControl.RegisterGroup(myGroupTag, group, out groupRelay); ProcessControl.RegisterWithGroup(myGroupTag, someProcess, out relay);

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.HomeRespawnPlace
files.Summary: Where the entity stood as it registered: its spawn. Where it never stood anywhere, where it died.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IAbilityProxyStagePolicy
files.Summary: How a stage's tasks end it: the compiler maps each to a sequence's stage policy, Any to the first task's end and All to every task's (AbilitySequenceCompiler). The legacy execution that awaited one itself is gone.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IAbilityReach
files.Summary: How far from its caster an ability's target may be: a capability an ability's component implements, as Cast Range does. The targeting tasks that search from their caster, the Creator Lab's bots and a game's own code ask an ability's reach through , never the component, so a reach of your own is asked as Cast Range is. A component that reaches enforces its reach itself, as Cast Range refuses a target beyond it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IAbilityValidationRule
files.Summary:
A rule an ability's activation keeps, for its source or its target. It took the generic IValidationRule, which nothing else took; it declares its own Validate.

A rule is a question, asked as often as the activation needs it answered: as it's requested, each frame a buffered request waits, and again once targeting has found its target, as the caster may have changed meanwhile. So a rule changes nothing and draws nothing: one that rolled a chance rolled it each time it was asked.

Validate checks the entity getSource hands it: the caster among an ability's Caster Checks, the target among its Target Checks. Refused, it says why in error, as "Hale's Health, 80, isn't < 50". A kind says which of the two it belongs among with .

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IAttributeImpactCarrier
files.Summary: Attribute impact carriers are sources of attribute impact (impact carriers)

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IAttributeImpacter
files.Summary:
A single magnitude-evaluation unit owned by an . One carrier may expose many impacters; the cached attribute aggregator walks them and applies their contributions in op-precedence order:

  1. — summed first → DirtyValue.
  2. — composed via .
  3. — added after multiplies.
  4. — wins (resolved by ).

Reversal under recompute model — retained carriers reverse automatically when removed (Recompute simply walks the new shorter retention list). One-shot committed contributions persist via CachedAttributeValue.committedOneShotDelta and are reversed only by an explicit synthetic-carrier rollback (see GameplayEffectImpact.ReverseImpactOnRemoval).

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IAuraComponent
files.Summary: A component that holds an aura: its holder's effect on those near it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ICameraShaker
files.Summary: The game's camera, which a camera shake cue asks to shake.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ICarrierApplication
files.Summary:
The "applicable" facet of a carrier — duration, container generation, contained effects, worker phases, validation. exposes its application surface against this interface (not against a concrete ) so any future carrier kind that participates in the apply-shelf pipeline can plug in without subclassing the spec.

Plain s — synthetic deltas, leveler snapshots, nullified markers — intentionally do NOT implement this interface. They are identity + magnitude only; forcing them to expose duration policy or worker hooks would be lying about their lifecycle.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IComponentValidationRule
files.Summary: A check an ability's component stands behind, whatever the component's kind.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ICooldownModel
files.Summary: How an ability's uses come back: how many it holds, how many are in hand, and what a use spends. A capability an ability's component implements, as Charges does; with none, an ability has , one use, back as its Cooldown ends. The Cooldown check asks it what's in hand, an ability spends a use through it as it commits, and a HUD reads it through , whatever the ability's components are.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IEffectOrigin
files.Summary: Sources of Gameplay Effects

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IForgeClock
files.Summary: A source of time, which PlayForge's runtime reads instead of Unity's Time. The default reads Unity's; a test, a replay or a server puts one of its own in with . A sequence or a packet can name one of its own too (, ), as a menu's runs on .

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IForgeEntityIds
files.Summary: Names the entities a save refers to besides the one it's of: the source of an effect another entity applied. A game keeps IDs that last across sessions, as a reference doesn't.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IForgeInput
files.Summary: What click targeting reads of the player's input: whether a pointer's button went down this frame, and the ray the pointer aims along. The defaults read a mouse, a pen or a touch through a camera; a game with a gamepad's reticle, a controller's ray or input of its own puts its own in with . The Creator Lab and the task sequence libraries' waits read the keys and the pointer through it too.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IForgeMover
files.Summary: A game's own mover, as the Creator Lab's units are, which PlayForge's movement tasks tell what they do: a Dash holds it while it moves its entity, and a Blink stops it after it puts its entity elsewhere, so it drops the path it was on. A component on the entity's object that implements it hears; an entity without one moves as the task puts it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IForgeRandom
files.Summary: A source of random numbers, which PlayForge's runtime reads instead of UnityEngine.Random. The default reads Unity's, so Random.InitState still seeds it; is one of its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IForgeTurner
files.Summary: A game's own turner, on an entity's object: it turns its character itself, by its animation or its controller, as each step of a turn PlayForge orders asks, in place of PlayForge, which sets the entity's facing straight. PlayForge reads how far is left to turn from the entity's facing, its object's rotation, so that's what the turner turns.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IHasTextures
files.Summary: What holds textures under tags, as an asset's Textures: an ability, an item, an effect, an entity or a running one. An effect that inherits its texture takes its origin's under a tag.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ILevelProvider
files.Summary:
Interface for assets that can provide level information to linked effects. Implemented by Ability and EntityIdentity to support "Lock to Source" level mode.

When a GameplayEffect is linked to an ILevelProvider, the effect's modifiers can derive their MaxLevel from the provider, ensuring consistent scaling.

Common use cases:

  • Ability Cost effect linked to its parent Ability
  • Ability Cooldown effect linked to its parent Ability
  • Entity-specific effects linked to EntityIdentity

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.INumberWorker
files.Summary:
A worker that answers numbers: a number of the Worker kind, or an Asset Part number's Worker Value, asks it for a value under a key, and it answers from what it knows, as how much health its effect's target has lost since the effect began. Any worker can implement it: an effect's workers answer about their effect, and an entity's workers, those its worker groups give it, about the entity. Every number field can ask, so a worker can drive an effect's magnitude, a task's range, a threshold or a cue's parameter.

The context it's asked in is what it's asked about: for an effect's worker, the effect's own context, whose is the effect's spec, where its state for that application is (); for an entity's worker, the asking number's context. It answers false for a key it doesn't know, and the asker reads its default.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IPooledCue
files.Summary: What a pooled cue object does as its pool hands it out and takes it back, as Unreal's cue actors recycle: a MonoBehaviour on the prefab resets itself here, as a particle system that plays again from the start.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IProxyTaskBehaviourCaller
files.Summary: The system calling the composite behaviour

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.IRootAction
files.Summary: Interface for deferred actions that execute at end-of-frame. Actions can be invalidated (e.g., effect removed) before execution.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ISequenceInjection
files.Summary: An action that can modify sequence execution at runtime.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ISequenceStagePolicy
files.Summary: Determines how a stage completes based on its tasks.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ISequenceTask
files.Summary: Unified interface for tasks that can be executed within a TaskSequence. Supports both async execution (via Execute) and synchronous per-frame stepping (via Step). Task authors implement whichever path(s) their task will be used under.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ImpactSeries
files.Summary: Per-level evaluation of one impact entry: the magnitude the entry contributes at each level, and the total delivered over the effect's lifetime (ticks × magnitude for Periodic delivery).

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ImpactWorkerCache
files.Summary: Cache for impact workers, indexed by impacted attribute. Supports both inline and deferred execution modes.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ImpactWorkerContext
