files.Summary: Context for impact workers.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ImpactWorkerRun
files.Summary: One of a hit's dealer's impact workers, run for the hit, as the dealer tells it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.InputSystemPointerInput
files.Summary: The Input System's pointer, a mouse, a pen or a touch, aimed through a camera: the one given, or else Camera.main. A mouse presses each of its three buttons, and a pen or a touch the primary.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.InterruptSequenceInjection
files.Summary: Interrupts the entire sequence.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Item
files.Summary: ScriptableObject defining an item that can be added to an entity's inventory. Items can grant effects, abilities, and tags when equipped. Supports level scaling for linked effects and abilities.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ItemComponentContext
files.Summary: What an item's component hears a moment of its item with.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ItemSave
files.Summary: An item the entity holds.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ItemSpec
files.Summary: Runtime specification for an item instance. Contains the item's current state, level, and provides level information for linked effects/abilities.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ItemSpecContainer
files.Summary: Container that manages an item instance's lifecycle. Tracks equipped state, applied effects, abilities, and granted tags. Handles equip/unequip operations with proper cleanup.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ItemStacksScaler
files.Summary: The stack count of the item that applied the effect: 1 for an item that doesn't stack, and 1 for an effect no item applied. With Multiply With Scaler, an item's effect grows by the stack, as a relic of +10 a stack does. Nothing read an item's stack count.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ItemSystemCallbacks.ItemConsumedDelegate
files.Summary: Items used up, as a Consume Item task's, the item and how many went.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ItemSystemCallbacks
files.Summary: Callbacks for item system events. Used for monitoring item lifecycle without modifying behavior.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.JumpToStageInjection
files.Summary: Jumps to a specific stage by index.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.CreatorLab
files.Summary:
The Creator Lab: a space where an author puts units down, gives them their project's abilities, effects and items, casts, and watches the numbers move. It builds what it needs as it wakes: PlayForge, where the scene has none; the ground, a light and its camera; a world of its own, which it steps by its own time; its own caster, a neutral source for what the author drops; and its panels.

Window → PlayForge → Creator Lab opens it in a new scene. A test makes one with and drives it through the same calls the panels make.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.ELabStopKind
files.Summary: What a stop watches for.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.ELabWatchKind
files.Summary: What a watch reads.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.Editor.CreatorLabMenu
files.Summary: Window → PlayForge → Creator Lab: the lab in a new scene, played. The scenes open first are saved if the author wants. In the editor the lab lists every asset of the project, and opens one in The Forge.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.Editor.EditorLabLibrary
files.Summary: The library in the editor, by kind: the active Forge Project's assets, as The Forge's pickers offer them, or every asset of the project's own folders while it has no Forge Project; it switches the active project, as The Forge does, and follows as The Forge switches it. Given folders, it plays those folders' assets alone.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.Editor.LabDriverEditor
files.Summary: A Lab Driver's inspector, a project's own among them: the shared header, then its fields.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.Editor.LabRulesEditor
files.Summary: The Creator Lab's rules' inspector: the shared header, then their fields.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.ILabLibrary
files.Summary: The assets the lab plays: in the editor every PlayForge asset of the project or of its active Forge Project, in a build those a project names. The library panel lists them by kind.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.ILabRules
files.Summary: What the lab needs to know of a project to play its units: the attribute that is a unit's health, the one it walks at, the tags that stop, hide or shield it, where its attack range is kept, and which of its abilities is its attack. PlayForge has no movement or health of its own, so a project says which of its attributes are these. The Demo's roster says the same of the Demo.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.ILabUnitDriver
files.Summary: How a unit the author controls is ordered about: moved to a point, set on a unit to attack, made to cast, stopped. PlayForge has no movement of its own, so a project whose units move and cast their own way gives its own driver, on its Lab Rules, and the lab's controls and the Demo's give their orders through it. Without one, the lab's: a unit walks in a straight line and casts as the lab's units do.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabAssetKind
files.Summary: The kinds of asset the lab's library lists, in its order.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabAssets
files.Summary: What the lab knows of an asset of each kind: its kind, its name, its color.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabBlow
files.Summary: A blow a dummy took: when, how much, of what types, and from which effect.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabBodyDriver
files.Summary: The lab's own driver: its units walk in straight lines, set on a target, and cast as the lab's do.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabBot
files.Summary:
A bot's mind, the Demo's AI and the Battle sample's fighters made general: it takes the nearest foe it can target, casts what's ready in its order when its moment fits, handing its target in the activation's data, which click targeting takes with no click, and otherwise attacks. Low, it backs off a moment once in a while.

Its order is its entity's Local Data under the rules' cast order key, as "W Q E", the letters its casts in its entity's order; with none, each in turn. An ability's moment is its Local Data under the rules' cast-when key: InRange, the default, within its Cast Range, or else its Local Data reach, 0 for anywhere; Hurt, below 60% health; Low, below 35%, cast away from its foe, as an escape; Stunned, while something stops it; FoeLow, with its foe below half.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabCamera
files.Summary: The lab's camera: it looks down at an angle at a point on the ground, from the distance and tilt it's set to. Scroll pulls it back, a middle drag pans it, and puts it back as it started. It follows a unit when given one, as the Demo's follows its hero, and shakes as a cue asks, as the game's camera shaker PlayForge's cues reach through ForgeCues.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabControls
files.Summary: A player's controls for one unit, as a MOBA's: right-click the ground to move, right-click a foe it can target to attack it, Q, W, E and R for its abilities past its attack, 1 to 6 for its items' abilities, S to stop, Escape to cancel a cast. An ability that needs a target waits for a left-click, as its own click targeting reads it; meanwhile a ring on the ground shows the ability's reach, another ability's key casts that one instead, and a right-click order lets go of it. It reads PlayForge's input, ForgeInput, so a test or a game's own input stands in, and gives its orders through a driver: its own, its unit's rules', or the lab's. The Creator Lab's take its controlled unit; the Demo's player is these, its hero's.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabDriver
files.Summary: A project's driver as an asset: each order a virtual that does as the lab's does, so a project overrides those its game gives its own way, and names the asset on its Lab Rules. Create → PlayForge → Lab Driver.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabDummy
files.Summary: A test dummy, and the Demo's training dummy: a unit that stands and counts what it takes. It shows its damage a second over a window, the last blow with its types, and a short history of blows. It doesn't die unless asked: falling, it's revived where it stands at once. Left alone a few seconds, it mends to full, by the mend effect given, or else one of the lab's own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabEffects
files.Summary: The effects the lab makes for itself, as an asset's inspector would fill one in: a dummy's mend, where the project gives none. Each lives in memory alone and goes with what made it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabMode
files.Summary: What the lab's space holds.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabPanels
files.Summary: The lab's panels, UI Toolkit over the space: the library on the left, the mode on the right with the selected over it, shown as something is selected and set aside by its tab, and the log at the bottom; each other panel collapses to a tab at its edge. The middle stays the space's. Over the space, each unit's bar, and a status at the top that clicks go through: what a cast waits for, what's selected, whom the author controls, and the keys for what can be done now. An asset dragged from the library and dropped on the space is the lab's to apply, cast or give. Neutral panels, Unity's own controls, and a type's color in its icon alone.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabRules
files.Summary: A project's rules for the Creator Lab, as an asset. An attribute left empty is the one playing its role in the project, Health or Movement Speed, or else found by its name among the project's: Health, and Movement Speed or Move Speed. With no asset, the lab makes one and finds both.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabRulesExtensions
files.Summary: The checks a unit's rules answer, in one place for the lab, its bots and the Demo.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabSeat
files.Summary: A bot's place in a battle: what it's made of, its side, its level and where it starts, and what the author gave it since, which a reset gives again as it makes the bot anew.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabShowing
files.Summary: What the lab watches its units for, and the journals it keeps while it does: its effect journal over every unit, its stops, which pause its world as one fires and say which, and its watches, sampled over the last minute of its time. The lab steps it after each step of its world.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabSide
files.Summary: A side a unit stands on in the lab: an affiliation tag, as its registration's data gives it, a name and the color of its ring.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabSides
files.Summary: The lab's sides: Blue and Red for a fight, Green and Gold for more teams, and Neutral, the side of no one, which the lab's own caster stands on. Each is an affiliation tag of the lab's own, made as it's first asked for.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabStop
files.Summary: A stop: what it watches for, on the selected unit or any, and what it names, an effect, an ability, a tag, or an attribute and a value. The lab's world pauses as one fires, and says which.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabSummary
files.Summary: The selected panel's lines: an asset's numbers level by level, as "−80/−120/−160 Health", and a unit's attributes and effects as they are now.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabUnit
files.Summary: A unit in the lab, and the Demo's hero: a GameplayAbilitySystem on a body of its own, which walks where it's sent, attacks what it's set on, casts its abilities and its items', and holds its items. Its attributes, tags, levels and Local Data are the GAS's; this is the space's side of it. Movement is the lab's, a straight line on the ground at its speed, as a project's own body would be for a game.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabUnitSpec
files.Summary: What a unit is made from, and where it stands.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabWatch
files.Summary: A watch: a unit's attribute, a tag's count, an effect's stacks or time, or a number read on it, pinned, and its values over the last minute of the lab's time, one each tenth of a second.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.ListLibrary
files.Summary: A library of the assets given, as a test or a build gives them.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LambdaAction
files.Summary: Simple action that executes a lambda. Use sparingly.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LazyMonoProcess
files.Summary: The Lazy process is a process (typically self-terminating) that runs until Waited or Terminated.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LegacyPointerInput
files.Summary: The Input Manager's mouse, aimed through a camera: the one given, or else Camera.main.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LevelCondition
files.Summary: Whether the level compares with a number: the level itself, or how far up its range it is, from 0 at its least to 1 at its most.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LevelSave
files.Summary: A level the entity keeps: its own, or an ability's or an item's, under that one's asset tag.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LevelSystemCallbacks
files.Summary: Callbacks for level system events. Used for monitoring level changes without modifying behavior.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LifestealImpactWorker
files.Summary: The Lifesteal worker: it heals its holder a share of each workable loss it deals another, the value of its holder's Share, the attribute it names, which an effect on the holder raises while it should. The losses that count are to its Receives attribute, and it heals its Heals attribute, each the Health role's where it names none. An effect has no lifesteal of its own. Only hits of the impact types it names count, as attacks, so a second worker on another attribute makes a spell vamp. A project gives it to every entity through its Forge Project's Workers, and an entity can hold one of its own; one that holds two heals a hit once. It allocates nothing, healing or not.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LineOfSightValidation
files.Summary: Line of Sight: nothing on the layers it names blocks a line from the caster to its target, run at a height above each, so the ground under them doesn't. The two ends' own colliders don't block it. The line runs between their targeting packets, so it's drawn for an entity of either hub, and 3D physics colliders block it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LinkedSourceAttribute
files.Summary: Attribute to mark fields that should use the LevelProviderDrawer. Apply to ScriptableObject fields that should only accept ILevelProvider types.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LocalAbility
files.Summary: An ability.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LocalAttribute
files.Summary: An attribute.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LocalBool
files.Summary: A bool.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LocalDataKind
files.Summary: A value in Local Data, under a key, as a hero's attack range: in what the number belongs to (the ability's or the item's asset, or an entity's own Local Data, where the number is the entity's), or in the caster's or the target's Local Data as the entity holds it at runtime. An entry that holds a float or a whole number reads as that number; where there's no number under the key, it reads its .

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LocalDataValue<T>
files.Summary: A Local Data value that holds one T, its , as most kinds do.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LocalDataValue
files.Summary: A Local Data entry's value. A kind holds its value as gives it, gives it as a packet takes it with , a number read where it's used, and says whether it's a number with , as a Local Data number and a tag rule read one. Most kinds hold one value, a 's.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LocalEffect
files.Summary: An effect.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LocalEntity
files.Summary: An entity's identity.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LocalFloat
files.Summary: A number that can scale, read where it's used: at the level and with the caster it's read for.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LocalInt
files.Summary: A whole number that can scale, read where it's used.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LocalMonoBehaviour
files.Summary: A component on a prefab, as a process to spawn.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LocalObject
files.Summary: Any asset, as a prefab or a material.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LocalScriptableObject
files.Summary: A ScriptableObject asset.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LocalString
files.Summary: A string.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.LocalTag
files.Summary: A tag; one left empty is none.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.MagnitudeSave
files.Summary: A magnitude a caller set under a tag.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.MainThreadSequenceTask
files.Summary: Task that executes a synchronous action on the main thread. Forces non-async execution by only accepting Action delegates.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.MathAttributeWorker
files.Summary: Performs math operations on attribute changes relative to another attribute. This is an INLINE worker because it modifies the ChangeValue directly.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ModifyAttributeAction
files.Summary: Deferred action to modify an attribute. One the system makes for itself, such as a rescale or a lifesteal's heal, is used again once the queue has run it, so a listener handed one reads it during the call.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.MultiplierVariance
files.Summary: The value times a multiplier between its Min and its Max, as 0.9 to 1.1.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.MultiplyStage
files.Summary: The value times a number read for the hit: a bonus, × Caster's Damage Amplification read as 1 + x; a reduction, × Target's Damage Resistance read as what's left; an armor curve; a bonus that reads the target, as Crowbar's above 90%.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.NeverCondition
files.Summary: A condition that never holds.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.NewAssetSettings
files.Summary: Where a type's new assets go. A new asset's file is its name alone: the file prefix and suffix are gone.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.NotCondition
files.Summary: Whether its condition doesn't hold. Where that condition can't be worked out, neither can this, so it doesn't hold either: not having a target's tag doesn't hold where there's no target.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.NumberComparison
files.Summary: A comparison between two numbers, as a condition makes one, and how a line writes it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.NumberContext
files.Summary:
What a number is read against: what its site has. A kind of number reads it; it is the whole of a kind's API, so adding to it later breaks no kind. It offers the caster, the target and the level; the carrier, where there is one, and what it has dealt; the caller's magnitudes and Local Data, each by key; an attribute's value or a retention group's part of it, on either side, and through the effects there; the activation's data, where a task reads it; and the owner, the object the field belongs to. says which of these this site provides.

A site builds one with Of, from an effect spec, a container, an activation's data, a worker's context, an entity, a cue or a process, and reads its numbers through it: Range.Evaluate(NumberContext.Of(data)). A test builds one with . It is a struct, and a number read through it allocates nothing.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.NumberContextAttribute
files.Summary: Says what a number field's context provides, which kinds its kind menu then offers, and which the Problems window flags. A targeting task's range has no target yet, as the target is what it looks for: [NumberContext(NumberReads.Level | NumberReads.Caster | NumberReads.Caller | NumberReads.LocalData)]. A field without it offers every kind but one that reads its owner, as an effect's numbers have everything else. An owner is given only by the code that reads the field, Max.Evaluate(context, this), so a field whose code gives one says so, [NumberContext(NumberReads.All)], and Relative to a Field joins its menu. It also takes the field's unit: a field whose unit is "%" stores 0.3 and shows and takes it as 30%.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.NumberKind
files.Summary:
A kind of number of your own: one class with one method. Override to work out the kind's value from what the context offers, and for the field's one-line summary. Name it, file it and say what it reads with , and the kind menu offers it in every number field whose context provides what it reads:

[Serializable]
[NumberKind("Distance to Target", Reads = NumberReads.Caster | NumberReads.Target)]
[ForgeMenu("Space", Description = "How far the target is from the caster")]
public class DistanceToTarget : NumberKind
{
    [Tooltip("Along the ground, leaving height out")]
    public bool Flat = true;

    protected override float Evaluate(in NumberContext context)
    {
        var from = context.Caster.GetTargetingPacket().position;
        var to = context.Target.GetTargetingPacket().position;
        if (Flat) from.y = to.y = 0f;
        return Vector3.Distance(from, to);
    }

    public override string Describe() => "the distance to the target";
}

A kind is a scaler, so it also works wherever a scaler does: inside a Group, a Conditional or a Clamped, and in an effect's magnitude. The base answers the scaler's carrier methods by building a and calling yours. It reads no values per level. Its fields draw in the inspector with no editor code, as a scaler's do, with [Tooltip] and [ForgeShowWhen].

A kind is saved by its class's name, so renaming the class needs Unity's [MovedFrom], as any [SerializeReference] value does. Test one without an effect through .

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.NumberKindAttribute
files.Summary: Names a kind of number in the kind menu and says what it reads of a field's context. Its place in the menu is its 's, as every kind's is: it named a Category of its own. The inspector offers the kind only in fields whose context provides what it reads, and the Problems window flags it where it's found in one that doesn't. Without it, a kind takes its class's name, as a scaler does, and is offered everywhere.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.NumberMaxAttribute
files.Summary: The most a number field's constant takes in the inspector: [NumberMax(10)]. With beside it, the field takes what lies between the two. See for what a limit reaches.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.NumberMinAttribute
files.Summary:
The least a number field's constant takes in the inspector, as Unity's [Min] is for a float:

[NumberMin(0)] public ScalableFloat Duration = 2f;

A number field takes these in place of Unity's [Min] and [Range]. Unity gives a field that has one of its own to that attribute's drawer, which draws "Use Min with float, int or Vector" where the number was, so the console names a number field that has one as scripts load.

The limit is the inspector's, as Unity's is: it keeps the constant typed in. A number of a kind is worked out as the game runs, so where what it reads must stay inside limits, give it the Clamped kind, or clamp what the code reads. On a field whose unit is "%" the limit is in what the field stores: [NumberRange(0, 1)] is 0% to 100%. A whole-number field takes the whole numbers inside the limits.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.NumberRangeAttribute
files.Summary: A number field whose constant is set on a slider between two values, as Unity's [Range] is for a float: [NumberRange(0, 1)] public ScalableFloat Chance = 0.5f;. See for what a limit reaches.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.NumberReads
files.Summary: What a number field's context provides: what a site has for its numbers to read, which tests, what a kind needs (), and what a field declares ().

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.NumberSiblingFieldAttribute
files.Summary: Marks the string field that names a relative number's sibling, which the inspector picks from a menu.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.NumberSide
files.Summary: Which of a context's two entities a read is about.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.NumberText
files.Summary: A number's one-line summary, as its field shows it under its row: "0.3 × Target's Health (base)", "Fire Duration + 2", "the caller's Data.Damage". A kind of your own gives its part through . A field whose unit is "%" reads its numbers as percentages: "30% × Target's Health (base)".

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.NumberTrace
files.Summary:
A number's read, explained: a tree of its parts, each with what it read and what it gave. A charged hit reads −180 because its Group adds its caster's Attack Damage, 100, to a Conditional that gives 80, as the caster's Combo Charges, 4, are above 0. A part whose context lacks what it reads says what it needs, "the target", and gives its fallback, so a read in the editor with no entities says where it would change in play.

Each part reads as the number does, through the same context, so the parts and the read agree. A read that rolls, as a Randomized scaler's, rolls again for its parts. A trace allocates, and is for the editor, tools and tests.

A kind or a condition of a project's own explains its parts by overriding or and adding them: trace.Add(Min, context, this, "Min").

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.NumberWorkers
files.Summary: The workers on each entity that answer numbers, and the way to ask them or an effect's workers. A worker group installs its workers that answer as it gives them to an entity, and takes them back with them; code that gives an entity a worker of its own can do the same with .

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.OnHitEntry
files.Summary: Effects that an item, an ability or an effect applies as its holder's hits land, or on the hit that kills: Desolator's armor, a dagger's bleed, a boon's Weak, a barrier on a kill. A hit is a loss to its Attribute, as Health, that the holder deals another entity: only of its impact types, where it names any, so a bleed's ticks, typed apart from attacks, set off nothing; and only while its condition holds. Each effect's own Chance to Apply rolls as it lands, and its hits set the entry off no more, so a shock it applies doesn't shock again. An item's hold while it's equipped, an ability's while it's known, an effect's while it lasts.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.OnHits
files.Summary: Gives a holder the On Hits it has, and takes them back.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.OriginSave
files.Summary: What applied an effect: an entity, or one of its abilities or items. is empty for the entity the save is of, and otherwise the ID an gives the other.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.PercentageVariance
files.Summary: Up or down by a share of the value, as 0.1 for 10% either way.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.PlayCueTask
files.Summary: Plays its cues' bursts at a stage's exact moment, as a sword's arc or a spell's release: on its caster, on its activation's target, or at its activation's point. A cue there hears the activation's data, and a magnitude read as it plays, for a cue to scale with. An ability's lifelong moments play through its Cues component.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.PointRespawnPlace
files.Summary: A point in the world.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.PrefabCue
files.Summary: Places a prefab where its placement says: a burst as its moment comes, gone after its Lifetime, or, in a Cues component's list of lasting cues, as an effect's While Active, for as long as its cue lasts. Its placement puts it on the one the cue is on, its source, an ability's target or each of its targets, or at the cue's point, as a hit's: at a socket, moved and scattered, following them while it lasts or as it says. Pooled, it takes its objects from and gives them back, as Unreal recycles its cue actors.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ProcessAttribute
files.Summary: An attribute a gameplay mono process carries of its own, as a projectile's speed: the attribute it is, the role the process reads it by, and where its value starts. It changes as the process runs.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ProcessControlBlock
files.Summary: Represents a managed process instance with state tracking and lifecycle management.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ProcessControlCallbacks
files.Summary:
Callbacks fired by for high-level observers (debuggers, recorders, GAS-aware observers, etc.).

These are in addition to the per-process ProcessWatcher system — watchers subscribe to a specific ProcessRelay, whereas callbacks fire for every process managed by ProcessControl.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ProcessCue
files.Summary: Runs a MonoBehaviour process where its placement says: a burst's runs its own course, and one in a list of lasting cues runs for as long as its cue lasts, as a shield's that ends as the shield goes. Each runs with a data packet loaded for the cue (), its Data list last, so the process reads the cue's entity, its asset and its numbers. Pooled, its objects come from through , and each goes back as its process ends.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ProcessDataPacket
files.Summary: ProcessDataPackets (and subclasses) contain data pertaining to processes and abilities Example usage: An ability, Cast, fires a ball that homes in on its target Cast is the ability and via implicit data and/or targeting tasks assigns some data to the packet The Ball is a MonoProcess and is created via ProcessControl Before initializing the MonoProcessWrapper is passed the data packet and its initial values are set After initializing the MonoProcess is passed the data packet It is responsible for procuring data from the data packet E.g. procuring the target transform via Data.TryGetPayload[Transform](Target, GameRoot.TransformParameter, Primary, out Transform value) This procures the Transform value under the Target classification stored under the key GameRoot.TransformParameter

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ProcessHierarchy.HierarchyNode
files.Summary: Represents a node in the process hierarchy. A node corresponds to a GameObject that has one or more processes.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ProcessHierarchy
files.Summary:
Manages hierarchical relationships between MonoProcesses. Parent actions cascade to children, but not vice versa.

Hierarchy Rules:

  • Processes on the SAME GameObject are "siblings" (treated as a group)
  • Processes on CHILD GameObjects are "children"
  • Only the FIRST ancestor with processes counts as the "parent"

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ProcessRegistration
files.Summary:
A process's registration with ProcessControl, built a step at a time: what handles the process, the packet it carries, the ProcessControl that takes it, and, for a MonoBehaviour process, what makes its object. and its siblings start one, and registers the process and starts it, as registering always has:

var result = ProcessControl.Register(projectile).HandledBy(gas).With(data).Run();
if (!result) Debug.Log(result.Refusal);

What isn't given takes its default. The handler follows the packet's run-time type: an ability's packet hands the process to its source, and any other to GameRoot, or to none in a world of its own, which reaches for nothing of the scene's. ProcessControl had 28 static Register overloads, and the argument's static type picked the handler, so an ability's packet passed as a SequenceDataPacket filed its sequence under GameRoot, and the sequence didn't end with its entity. Those overloads are wrappers of this now, marked obsolete, and go before the first Asset Store submission.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ProcessRegistrationResult
files.Summary: What a registration did: the relay of the process ProcessControl took, or why it refused it. It reads as true when the process was taken. A refused call returned false and a null relay, and said nothing of why.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ProcessRelay
files.Summary: Provides external access to ProcessControlBlock data without exposing internal state management.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ProcessWorld
files.Summary: The processes of one world and how they're stepped: every process's block, its step groups, the watches, the groups, which processes each GAS owns, the control state and its transitions, and the callbacks. A scene's ProcessControl wraps one and steps it from Unity's loop, and code can own one and step it itself, as a headless run does. It was ProcessControl itself, so no process ran without a ProcessControl in a scene.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ProjectileMonoProcess
files.Summary: A projectile: it flies at its target at its speed, the ProjectileSpeed role, and applies its effects as it lands. Its speed is an attribute it carries, or its origin's.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.PurgeContext
files.Summary: What a purge's filter reads an effect with.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.PurgeLevels
files.Summary: A project's purge levels: tiers of tags, weakest first, an effect at the first whose tag its asset tag or a context tag matches; a purge of a tier takes the effects at it or under it, and an effect at none is never purged, but by death. And the categories a death keeps whatever their tiers.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.PurgeTier
files.Summary: A tier of a project's purge levels: the tag an effect carries to be at it, and whether a death keeps it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.RandomizedScaler
files.Summary: Adds random variance to level-based scaling. Useful for damage ranges, proc chances, etc. Its variance is a class: by a share of its value, by an amount, between two multipliers, or a way of your own, as dice. A variance's numbers are of any kind, read with the variance as their owner, so a share can widen by level and a Max multiplier can be 3 × its Min.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ReadOnlyListView<T>
files.Summary: A read-only view of a list that foreach walks without allocating, through the list's own struct enumerator. Walked as an , as any list's, the enumerator is boxed.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.RelativeOperationContextImpactWorker
files.Summary: Impact worker that applies effects relative to the impact (e.g., lifesteal). Can be configured as INLINE (immediate) or DEFERRED (end-of-frame).

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.RelativeToFieldKind
files.Summary:
Another number field of the same object: the number joins it as its Combine says, times it or plus it, so a Clamped scaler's Max can be 2 × Min and a stack bound's Max Min + 3. The field is a number ( or ), read in the same context, so a relative Max follows a Min that scales by level, or a plain float or int.

It reads its object through the owner its object's own code gives as it reads its numbers, MaxValue.Evaluate(context, this), and a field whose code gives one declares in its . With no owner, with a field name its object no longer has, or in a loop of numbers that read each other, which stops 8 deep, its number reads its own value and logs once. It finds its field by name through an accessor made once for each type and field, so a read allocates nothing after the first.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.RemoveEffectAction
files.Summary: Deferred action to remove an effect.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.RepeatUntilSkippedPolicy
files.Summary: Stage repeats infinitely until explicitly skipped, interrupted, or broken. Maintained stages with this policy will continue repeating. Use BreakStageRepeatInjection to exit the repeat loop gracefully.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.RequirementTemplate
files.Summary:
A reusable tag requirement configuration that can be shared across multiple assets.

Usage:

  1. Create a RequirementTemplate asset (Create > PlayForge > Templates > Requirement Template)
  2. Configure the required/avoided tags in the template
  3. Reference this template from any requirement field using the "Link Template" button
  4. Changes to the template will propagate to all linked requirements when they sync

Note: Linked requirements can "break" the link to make local modifications.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ResolveOrderEntry
files.Summary: One entry of a project's resolve order: those carrying its tag, or one under it, resolve at its Order among an area's hits, lower first.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.RespawnEntityComponent
files.Summary: Respawn: revives an entity that stays as it dies a while after, in its own time, at its home, where it died, a point, or a place of your own, as a hero comes back at its fountain. Its Death's On Revive effects land as it does, as any revive's do; a revive before its time, as a buyback, ends the wait. The wait is its entity's , a service a HUD can read. An entity that ends as it dies has nothing to revive, which the Problems view says. An entity holds one at most.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.RespawnTimer
files.Summary: An entity's wait to revive, as its Respawn starts it: the time left, by the entity's own clock, and where it revives, at the end of the frame its time runs out. A revive before its time, as a buyback, ends the wait. A service of the entity, so a HUD reads it as gas.FindService<RespawnTimer>().

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.RetentionGroups
files.Summary: Which retention groups' parts an attribute read takes. An attribute's value is the sum of its groups' parts: the base its set gives, what items add in their group, what a buff adds in its. × Attribute, an Attribute condition, a Math worker's Relative To and a Threshold worker read the whole value unless they say otherwise: only these groups, as a bonus of the items' strength reads their group; or all but these, as a bonus of a hero's own damage leaves its items' out. A group names the groups under it too. Group Impact reads one group's part, as it did.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ReturnDamageAttributeWorker
files.Summary: Damage return: a share of each workable loss its attribute takes from another goes back to the one who dealt it, typed Returned, so no return returns it again and no lifesteal heals from it, as Blade Mail.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ReviveOnRemovalEffectWorker
files.Summary: Revives the entity its effect is on as the effect ends: a respawn timer, as a staying entity takes as it dies, whose duration is the time it waits. It revives where the entity was, or at a point. An entity revived already, as by a buyback, takes nothing from it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.RuntimeGameplayAbilitySystem
files.Summary:
Runtime (non-MonoBehaviour) version of GameplayAbilitySystem. Instantiated at runtime as a plain class. Derives from LazyRuntimeProcess and implements the same IGameplayAbilitySystem interface as the MonoBehaviour version. What makes it a GAS lives in , which it builds in its constructor and forwards to.

Usage: var gas = new RuntimeGameplayAbilitySystem(entityData); var relay = ProcessControl.Register(gas).With(dataPacket).Run().Relay;

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ScalableFloat
files.Summary:
An authored gameplay number. It is a plain number by default, and it can also be one of the kinds the inspector's kind menu offers: a value by level, a multiple of an attribute, a value its caller sets, any scaler, or a kind a project writes (). It is the magnitude field it grew from, under a new name, with the same saved fields: its number (), its scaler, and how the two combine (). So every magnitude saved before it loads as it was.

A float converts to one, so public ScalableFloat Range = 20f; and effect.Range = 5f; compile. There is no conversion back, as it would drop the kind: a read is , once, at the site's natural moment, as an effect as it's applied or a task as it starts.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ScalableInt
files.Summary: A whole gameplay number: for counts, as an effect's ticks or a stack's size. It takes every kind a does, and rounds what it reads as says, so a kind is written once. It is the whole-number magnitude field it grew from, with the same saved fields.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ScaledClock
files.Summary: A time scale of its own over another clock, its source: a sequence on it runs at its scale, as a finisher's slow motion or a flourish at double speed, and the sequences that share one slow, speed up or stop together as it's set. Its source is the clock given, or, with none, the clock in force: the game's, or a world's or a tick's while one steps.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ScaledClockChoice
files.Summary: A pace of its own over another clock, as a finisher's slow motion at half or a flourish at double: a of its scale, made for each run, over the clock its Of picks, or the caster's.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ScalerAsset
files.Summary: A scaler kept as an asset of its own, which scaler fields reference through a . Editing it changes every field that uses it, so nothing propagates; a field adjusts it only through its own Magnitude, as in Fire Duration × 1.5. It was the Scaler Template, whose link code had no callers, so reuse meant copying a scaler into each field and propagating edits by hand.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ScalerDisplayName
files.Summary: Explicitly sets the display name for a Scaler field. Takes precedence over DeriveScalerName.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ScalerGroup
files.Summary:
Several numbers joined as one: each member is a scaler or a kind of number, and says how it joins the others. Members that add are added up; that sum is multiplied by each member that multiplies and divided by each that divides; then each flat bonus is added on. So (5 + Caster's Strength) × 2 + 3 is one number, a wind-up's 1.7 ÷ Caster's Attack Speed another, and a curse's 5 + what its worker answers is one magnitude.

A member that overrides gives the group's value alone. Where several override, picks among them: the highest, the lowest, their average, the first or the last; Ignore sets them aside, and the other members join as they would without them.

Each member reads in the number's own context, so a member that is a kind reads all the field's context gives, and a member that is a scaler evaluates against the effect, or against the carrier the context fills where there's no effect. Joining its members allocates nothing.

It reads its members alone, so it has no values per level. With no members, or none that holds a kind, it is no kind at all (): its field reads its number, as a field with no kind does. It read values per level of its own, which its inspector hid.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ScalerImpacter
files.Summary:
The default impacter shape — wraps a (the editor-authored magnitude + scaler + RealMagnitude triplet that already lives on ) and exposes it through the impacter contract.

One per is the current shape.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ScalerOperationKeyword
files.Summary:
Specifies a keyword that customizes labels in ScalableFloat and ScalableInt property drawers.

The keyword is used to:

  • Set the magnitude label to "Base {Keyword}" or "Additional {Keyword}"
  • Set the operation label to "Real {Keyword}" or "Use {Keyword}"
  • Set the scaler label to "{Keyword} Scaler" (via DeriveScalerName)

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SeededRandom
files.Summary: Random numbers of their own, from a seed, which nothing else draws from: two runs from one seed draw the same numbers, whatever else in the game draws from Unity's.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SelectDirectionTargetTask
files.Summary:
Interactive targeting task: click to define a direction from the caster. Raycasts from the camera to determine the world position clicked, then computes a normalized direction from the caster to that point.

Stores the direction in Tags.TARGET_POS as a Vector3 and the clicked world position in Tags.POSITION. Useful for skill shots, dashes, line attacks, etc.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SelectGasOrPositionTargetTask
files.Summary: Interactive targeting task: raycast to select either a GAS target or a world position. Prioritizes GAS targets (ITarget) — if the hit object has no ITarget component, falls back to using the hit position. Tag requirements apply only to GAS targets.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SelectGasTargetInRangeTask
files.Summary:
Interactive targeting task: click to select a GAS target within range. Like SelectGasTargetTask, but adds a maximum distance check from the caster to the clicked target. Invalid targets outside range trigger retry or failure.

Useful for melee abilities, short-range spells, or any ability where the player must select a target within a specific radius.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SelectGasTargetTask
files.Summary: Interactive targeting task: raycast to select a GAS target (ITarget). Waits for the player to click on a valid target in the world. Validates the hit object has an ITarget component and passes tag requirements.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SelectPositionTargetTask
files.Summary: Interactive targeting task: raycast to select a world position. Waits for the player to click on a valid surface in the world. Stores the hit position in the data packet under Tags.POSITION.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SendEventTask
files.Summary: Sends a gameplay event to its caster, or to each of its activation's targets, as a combo's hit tells its next stage it connected, or as an ability sets off another's trigger. The event's data holds its caster as Source and the one it's sent to as Event Subject, with the activation's caller's magnitudes; it's sent at once, and the abilities it triggers try to activate as a trigger's do.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SequenceAnnotation
files.Summary:
Declarative annotation of what a sequence DOES — the introspection channel for code-driven sequences. Sequence bodies are opaque async lambdas; annotations let the author state gameplay intent so can decipher abilities built on RunSequenceTask (tooltips, the Forge analysis tab, debugging).

The load-and-apply pattern: an asset-loader task (e.g. SetEffectsTask) puts effects into the data packet under a tag, and the sequence applies them via data.TryApplyEffects(target, tag). Annotating with that tag () lets the inspector connect the loaded effect assets to this sequence's application — including how many times (, e.g. Chain Lightning's 4 jumps).

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SequenceCondition
files.Summary: A condition that triggers an injection when met.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SequenceCue
files.Summary: Runs a task sequence on a data packet loaded for the cue (), its Data list last, so the sequence reads the cue's entity, its asset and its numbers: a burst's runs its course, and one in a list of lasting cues runs until its cue ends, as a shield's flicker that stops as the shield goes. It runs in the world of the one it plays on, by the clock its Clock picks, else the sequence's own, else its owner's.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SequenceDataPacket
files.Summary: Extended ProcessDataPacket for TaskSequence execution. Provides direct access to sequence, stage, and chain control. All TaskSequence builder methods use this type for delegates.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SequenceEventContext
files.Summary: Context passed to sequence event callbacks.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SequenceInfo
files.Summary: A code-driven sequence referenced by a RunSequenceTask, with its declared behavior.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SequenceMetadata
files.Summary: Optional metadata for the sequence.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SequenceStage
files.Summary: A stage within a TaskSequence containing tasks and/or sub-stages.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SequenceStageMetadata
files.Summary: Optional metadata for a stage.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SequenceTaskBase
files.Summary: Base class for async-first sequence tasks. Execute is abstract (must implement). Step defaults to instant completion (returns true). If you need your task to work in synchronous sequences, override Step.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SequenceTaskLibrary
files.Summary:
Reusable async building blocks for common gameplay operations. Designed to be awaited inside TaskSequence .Task() lambdas where the caller has access to the data packet and cancellation token.

Usage: .Task(async (d, t) => { var target = d.GetPrimary<Transform>(Tags.TARGET); await Seq.MoveTo(target, Vector3.zero, 1.5f, t, easeCurve); })

All timed methods:

  • Accept an optional AnimationCurve for easing (null = linear)
  • Snap to the final value after completion to avoid float drift
  • Respect CancellationToken for interrupt/skip/timeout support
  • Handle zero/negative duration by snapping immediately
  • Hold while their sequence is paused, given the token the task was handed. ArcForce can't: physics moves the body whatever the sequence is doing

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SetBonusItemComponent
files.Summary: Set Bonus: an effect its holder has while it has enough of a set's pieces equipped, as two pieces of a set giving fire resistance and four a flame aura. Each piece names its set by a tag and carries the set's bonuses; the holder's equipped pieces count each item once, and a bonus holds while they're as many as it needs, once for the holder however many pieces carry it. An item holds one for each of its set's bonuses.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SetByCallerScaler
files.Summary:
A value the caller passes in under a tag, as Unreal's SetByCaller is: code that knows the amount as it applies an effect or activates an ability sets it, and the number reads it.

What it checks: whether the context it's read in holds a value under exactly . A context holds the values set on what it was built from: an effect's spec (spec.SetByCaller(tag, value), before it's applied), an ability activation's data (data.SetByCaller(tag, value), which each effect the ability makes takes as it's made, and which the ability's tasks read), or the data that spawned a process. Only the key itself matches: a value set under a tag above or below it in the tag tree doesn't. A value set to 0 is a value, and is read. Where the context holds no value under the key, or holds no values at all, as an entity on its own, it reads .

It is a number kind, so it reads from any context that holds values: it read only an effect spec's, so a task's or a process's number read its default. Its default is a number of any kind, read with the scaler as its owner, so where nothing is set it can read a value by level.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SharedCachedScaler
files.Summary: An attribute set's reference to a shared whose scaler is one of the cached kinds: it reads the asset's scaler as the entity's values change, so an edit to the asset reaches every element that uses it. It keeps no values of its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SharedScaler
files.Summary: A field's reference to a shared : it reads the asset's scaler, so an edit to the asset reaches every field that uses it, with nothing to propagate. It keeps no values of its own; the field's Magnitude adjusts what it reads, as in Fire Duration × 1.5.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ShownWhenAttribute
files.Summary: A kind's field shown only while another field of the same object says so: a toggle that's on, or, given values, an enum or a whole number that's one of them, as a targeting task's Detection Layers under Use Physics. A kind field, as a task's or a scaler's, draws its object's fields with this read, hiding one where it doesn't apply; it shows again as the field it reads changes.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SideChangeEffectComponent
files.Summary: Side Change: while its effect lasts, its target's sides are its caster's, as they are as it lands, a mind control, or those it names, as a pacify's Neutral. Of several on one entity, the highest Priority holds, a tie going to the latest, and the entity's own come back as the last ends. One that interrupts breaks what its target runs as it changes the side, landing or ending. An Instant effect doesn't last, so it changes nothing. An effect holds one at most. It was a field of the effect's own, with a switch.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SideSet
files.Summary: The side changes an entity is under, each from an effect that lasts: the sides the highest Priority gives, a tie to the latest, or none, where its own hold.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SimpleScaler
files.Summary: Simple level-based scaler that evaluates based on relative level. Uses the level values array for easy configuration.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SingleCooldown
files.Summary: The single cooldown, an ability's cooldown model where none of its components gives another: one use, spent as its Cooldown is applied, and back as the Cooldown ends, as its caster no longer carries the Cooldown's asset tag.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SkipAndMaintainInjection
files.Summary: Skips the current stage but maintains it running in background.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SkipStageInjection
files.Summary: Skips the current stage and moves to the next.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SoundCue
files.Summary: Plays a sound where its placement says, as its moment comes, in whichever list it's in: on the one the cue is on, its source, an ability's target or each of its targets, or at the cue's point; attached, it follows them as it plays.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SpreadEffectComponent
files.Summary: Spread: spreads its effect, or another it names, from the one it's on to those near them, at the moments it names: as it lands, each tick, as it ends, or as the one it's on dies, as a plague jumps from its victim to the enemies near it. Each it takes gets the effect from the same origin, its caster's, so its modifiers and its chance to land are its own. A landing by spread spreads on only so far as its Hops allow.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.StackingCurveKind
files.Summary: A count through a stacking curve, then a number added: an item's stacks, an effect's stacks or an attribute, read as its curve says. Risk of Rain's items stack this way, and Dota's armor, so a number that reads stacks or armor needs no worker of its own. Plus 1 makes a share a multiplier.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.StacksChange
files.Summary: Changes its stacks: more it can hold at most, and more a landing gives.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.StandardWorkerGroup
files.Summary: A named group of workers that can be attached to entities, abilities, items, or attribute sets. Workers are disbursed to the appropriate subsystems when the owning asset is applied.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.StopMaintainedAllInjection
files.Summary: Stops all maintained stages.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.StopMaintainedAtIndexInjection
files.Summary: Stops the maintained stage at a stage index. A stage that isn't maintained, the current one among them, is left alone.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.StopMaintainedLastInjection
files.Summary: Stops the oldest maintained stage.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SyncSequenceStage
files.Summary: A stage containing one or more ISequenceTask instances driven synchronously. All tasks Step in parallel each frame; stage completes per its policy.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SyncSequenceTaskBase
files.Summary: Base class for sync-first sequence tasks (per-frame stepping). Step is abstract (must implement). Execute bridges automatically by looping Step with per-frame yields.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SyncSequenceTaskLibrary
files.Summary:
Reusable synchronous building blocks for common gameplay operations. Each method returns an ISequenceTask that advances per-frame via Step(). Also usable in async sequences — the DelegateSyncTask.Execute bridge loops Step automatically. Designed for use with TaskSequenceBuilder.

Usage: var runner = TaskSequenceBuilder.Create("Chase") .Stage(s => s .Task(SyncSeq.MoveTowards(chaser, target, 5f)) ) .BuildSyncRunner();

All timed tasks:

  • Accept an optional AnimationCurve for easing (null = linear)
  • Snap to the final value on completion to avoid float drift
  • Handle zero/negative duration by completing immediately

All tracking tasks (MoveTowards, LookAtTracking, etc.):

  • Re-sample the target each frame for dynamic following
  • Complete based on distance/condition, not duration

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.SyncedTaskSequence
files.Summary:
Drives a list of synchronous sequence stages frame-by-frame. Uses the unified ISequenceTask interface (calls Step on each task). Designed to be called from a process's WhenUpdate.

Usage: var runner = TaskSequenceBuilder.Create("MyRunner") .Stage(s => s.Task(...)) .BuildSyncRunner();

// In WhenUpdate, a step of its clock, or of a time given: if (runner.Step(data)) relay.Terminate();

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Tag
files.Summary: Represents a gameplay tag with hierarchical support using dot notation. Example: "Status.Debuff.Burn" where "Status" is the root, "Debuff" is a child, and "Burn" is the leaf.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TagCache
files.Summary: Manages tag state and tag workers for an entity. Supports hierarchical tag matching with O(1) exact lookups and O(n) hierarchical lookups. Tag worker activation/resolution is deferred to end-of-frame.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TagChange
files.Summary: A tag's weight on an entity changing: the tag, and its weight before and after, 0 when it isn't held. An event carries one as it happens; a compile, which rebuilds the tags from their sources, carries only what it changed.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TagCondition
files.Summary: Whether the caster or the target holds a tag: counted by weight, so a tag granted twice counts twice, on either side. It reads the side it looks at, so a target's tag doesn't hold where there's no target.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TagCue
files.Summary: Plays what a cue tag routes to, in place of naming what it shows: the entity's own Cue Receiver's way, or the project's cue library's, as Unreal's GameplayCue tags play their notifies. Each burst, beginning and end it hears plays the tag's.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TagListener
files.Summary: A listener on one tag of an entity and the tags under it, as makes: it hears Status.Burning when it listens to Status. Dispose stops it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TagQuery
files.Summary: Represents a query condition for a tag, with support for hierarchical matching. Used to validate whether an entity has/doesn't have certain tags.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TagRegistry
files.Summary:
Runtime registry for hierarchical tags. Provides O(1) lookups for parent/child relationships by maintaining cached mappings. Thread-safe for read operations.

Usage:

  • Tags are automatically registered when created via Tag.Generate()
  • Use TagHierarchy.GetChildren(), GetDescendants(), etc. for fast hierarchy queries
  • Call TagHierarchy.Initialize() at game start to pre-populate from known tags

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TagWorkerActivateAction
files.Summary: Deferred action to activate a tag worker.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TagWorkerResolveAction
files.Summary: Deferred action to resolve (deactivate) a tag worker.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TaggedCueWatch
files.Summary: An entity's While Tagged cues: each step, a tag the entity has taken on begins its cues, and one it has let go of ends them; as the entity ends, every one still playing ends.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TaggedCues
files.Summary: The lasting cues an entity plays while it holds a tag.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Tags
files.Summary: PlayForge's own tags, grouped by kind. Each is its text padded to 64 characters by a hash of it, a name every asset that uses the tag stores, so a text changed is another tag; a test pins each one's name and kind. Each is exposed to the editor's pickers for its kind.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TargetAttributeCondition
files.Summary: A single attribute condition used to filter auto-targeting candidates. Checks the target's current attribute value against a threshold.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TargetAttributeRatioThresholdEffectWorker
files.Summary: A threshold on an attribute's ratio, its Current to its Base, as below half its health: the ratio against Threshold's Current, whatever Target says, as a ratio has no other side. Its Base target compared Base to Base, which is always one; and with no Base there's no ratio, so no threshold is met.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TaskSequence
files.Summary: A reusable async task sequence that can be executed with a data packet. Wraps a TaskSequenceDefinition with execution capabilities.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TaskSequenceBuilder
files.Summary: Fluent builder for creating TaskSequence definitions. All delegate methods use SequenceDataPacket for direct sequence/stage control.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TaskSequenceChain
files.Summary: A chain of sequences that execute sequentially with shared data. Supports chain-level conditions, repeat, and interrupt.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TaskSequenceDefinition
files.Summary: The complete definition of a TaskSequence. Immutable after building. Can be reused across multiple runs.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TaskSequenceMethodAttribute
files.Summary: Marks a static method as a TaskSequence/TaskSequenceChain provider.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TaskSequenceProcess
files.Summary:
Wraps a TaskSequence or TaskSequenceChain for execution via ProcessControl. Supports both async (SelfTerminating/RunThenWait) and sync (Synchronous) lifecycles.

Async mode: RunProcess executes the sequence via Execute path. Sync mode: RunProcess is skipped; WhenUpdate drives the SyncedTaskSequence runner via Step path.

Uses SequenceDataPacket for direct sequence/stage control.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TaskSequenceReference
files.Summary: Serializable reference to a TaskSequence method.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TaskSequenceRuntime
files.Summary: Manages the runtime execution state of a TaskSequence. Created per-run, handles stage progression, injections, and cancellation.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TemplateListSnapshot
files.Summary: Stores the element identifiers of a list property at the time of last template sync. Used to detect additions/removals in the template for list merge logic.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.AllocationMarker
files.Summary: Runs after every other Update, so it marks where ProcessControl's stepping has finished and the test runner's coroutine tick is about to begin.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.AllocationProbe
files.Summary:
Measures allocation with , because the GC API returns 0 under Mono. Unity's "GC Allocated In Frame" counter reads live within a frame, so an operation is the counter's change across it. Dispose it as the test ends.

A frame takes more care, because the counter's own total for a frame is noisy: 450 to 532 bytes with nothing running, shifting at random. Sampling every player loop stage shows why. All of that lands outside the player loop, in the editor's work between frames, except 40 bytes from the test runner's coroutine tick. So a frame here is the counter's change from the player loop's first stage to its last, less that tick, measured on the same frame. A clean frame reads exactly 0, with no baseline to calibrate, and a baseline would be worse than noise: taken while the noise ran high, it would hide real allocation.

The cost is that anything allocated in a coroutine goes unmeasured with the test runner's. PlayForge's stepping runs in Update and its async work in UniTask continuations, which are measured.

Now and then a burst of a kilobyte or so landed on a few frames at random, whatever was running. It was the editor's Build Report REST service, which listens on a port of its own: where another editor holds that port, as one open beside a batch run does, it tries again about once a second on a thread of its own, and each try allocates about 4 KB, which the counter takes as the frame's. Most frames are short, so a try rarely landed in one, but among 500 entities, whose frames fill most of a second, nearly every measure took one. A probe ends those tries (). Other noise may still land, and it doesn't repeat, where real allocation does, so a measure that isn't clean is taken again and the cleanest stands. A leak fails every attempt.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.EffectConfig
files.Summary: What builds. Each field is the plain default unless a test needs otherwise.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.ForgeTest
files.Summary:
The base of a test that plays PlayForge content: a live before each test, and after it the world's invariants audited and the world ended. A test is a PlayMode [UnityTest] whose body runs through , from a frame's end:

[UnityTest]
public IEnumerator Burn_ticks_twice() => Live(async () =>
{
    var health = Make.Attribute("Health");
    var target = World.Entity(Hub.Runtime, Make.Set(Make.Pool(health, 100f, 100f)));
    var burn = Make.Effect("Burn", new EffectConfig { Policy = EEffectDurationPolicy.Durational, Target = health,
        Magnitude = -10f, Duration = 1f, PeriodicTicks = true, Ticks = 2 });
    World.Hit(World.Entity(Hub.Runtime), target, burn);
    await Frames.Until(() => World.Value(target, health) <= 80f, 90, "two ticks land");
});

A test with a base class of its own makes a world with instead.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.ForgeTestWorld
files.Summary:
One live PlayForge for one test: a real ProcessControl and GameRoot brought up by the real Bootstrapper, stepped by Unity's player loop a frame at a time. It makes what a test needs, entities on either hub, from an identity asset or from attributes, and plays them as a game does: applies an effect, gives an ability and starts it, starts one the entity has, and equips an item. Its and make time and chance the test's.

It ends as a test asks, or as it's disposed (await using): every process it began, every object and asset it made, and the framework's static state, so tests run in any order. first says what broke of its . makes one for each test, audits it and ends it. Step frames, and let ProcessControl step what runs: never call a process's update by hand.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.FrameAllocation
files.Summary: What a run of frames allocated.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.FramePulse
files.Summary: Counts the phases Unity ran, so can show a frame was a whole one.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.FrameStepper
files.Summary:
Steps the real player loop a frame at a time, so a test can say "this takes exactly N frames". A step ends at the frame's last player loop stage, once FixedUpdate, Update and LateUpdate have all run, so a test only ever looks at finished frames.

Time is captured: every frame lasts exactly and runs one FixedUpdate, however fast the machine is. Unscaled time doesn't follow, so anything timed on it stays on the wall clock. WaitForEndOfFrame never resumes under -nographics, which is why a step waits on a player loop stage instead.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.Hub
files.Summary: The two GAS hubs, so a test can play its content on each.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.Invariants
files.Summary: What must hold after every test, whatever it did. checks these after each test, so a test gets them without asking, and a test about something else still catches a leak: every observed entity's attribute parts sum to its value, what each dealt is what its targets received, and no process is left running.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.ScriptedRandom
files.Summary: Rolls that come out as the test writes them, one after another and round again, and how many were drawn, as sets them. A chance below a roll misses, so 0 always lands and 0.99 almost never does.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.SteppingClock
files.Summary: A clock whose frames each take a fixed step, as sets one.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.TestAssets
files.Summary: Builds PlayForge's assets in code, for one test world: attributes, sets, identities, effects, items and abilities, each ready to use. Everything it makes is destroyed with the world, and the tag names it gives are unique within it. A game's own assets, loaded from the project, are the test's to load.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ThresholdAnalysisWorker
files.Summary: Analysis worker that triggers callbacks based on attribute thresholds.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ThresholdScaler
files.Summary: Returns values based on level thresholds. Useful for tier-based progression (e.g., Bronze/Silver/Gold ranks). Each tier's value and its default are numbers of any kind, as a share of the caster's attribute. A tier reads its number where the scaler is read, and the default with the scaler as its owner.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ToggleAbilityComponent
files.Summary: Toggle: an effect an ability turns on its caster with one use, paying its cost, and off with the next, starting its cooldown. It applies its ability's usage in the ability's place, waives the cost and the cooldown while its effect is on, so it can always turn off, and claims its effect as a Toggle's for a purge. As its holder forgets the ability, the effect comes off, where it stayed on. An ability holds one at most.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TrackedImpact
files.Summary: What a carrier's impacts came to: their total, the last of them, and how many. It kept a node for every impact on a list nothing walked, so an effect that ticked kept an allocation for every tick for as long as it lasted.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TrackedImpactKind
files.Summary:
What an effect has dealt: its last impact, its total, or how many impacts, as each effect spec tracks them once they land, after workers, so a blow reads as it landed, after the target's armor. Whose: this effect, the one whose number it is, as a burn that grows each tick by its own count; an effect on the caster or the target, by its asset, its containers summed, as a combustion consuming a burn's total; or every effect there tagged with a tag, summed. An impact is signed, so damage is negative; reads it as a size, as a heal of half a blow wants. Where nothing is tracked, as an effect that isn't on the target, it reads 0.

At its first application an effect has dealt nothing: its last impact and total are 0, and so is its count. An effect's magnitude is worked out as it's applied and again at each tick, so a number on its own count reads the ticks so far. A save restores an effect's time and stacks but not what it has dealt, so after a load its tracked impact starts again at 0.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TransferEffectComponent
files.Summary: Transfer: moves an amount from an attribute of its effect's caster or target to one of either, as the effect lands, each tick, or while it lasts, giving back as it ends; only what the giver has moves. An effect holds as many as it moves, each its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TurnToFaceAbilityComponent
files.Summary: Turn To Face: how this ability turns its caster to face its target or its point before its first stage, in place of its entity's Turns To Face; or, with Turns off, that it doesn't, as a cast behind the caster doesn't. An ability holds one at most.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TurnToFaceSettings
files.Summary: How an ability's activation turns its caster to face its target or its point before its first stage.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TurnsToFaceEntityComponent
files.Summary: Turns To Face: every ability of the entity with a target or a point turns it to face it before its first stage, which starts once it's within the Start Angle; the turn goes on to the Facing Angle after. An ability with a Turn To Face of its own turns its own way, or not at all. An entity holds one at most.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.TypeDefaults
files.Summary: A type's defaults: the asset a new one starts as a copy of, and the assets Import lists first.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.UnityClock
files.Summary: Unity's time, the clock PlayForge reads unless another is put in.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.UnityRandom
files.Summary: Unity's random numbers, the source PlayForge reads unless another is put in.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.UnscaledClock
files.Summary: The game's time without its time scale, as the clock in force reads it: a sequence on it runs while the game is slowed or stopped, as a pause menu's or a hit-stop's own effects do. Its sequences wait for Unity's frames where the game's ticks would stand with the game's time.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.UnscaledClockChoice
files.Summary: The game's time without its time scale: a sequence on it runs while the game is paused.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.UsesItemComponent
files.Summary: Uses: how many times an item's ability can be used, each use one that paid what it costs, as a potion's sips or a wand's charges. With none left, one of the item goes: a stack of it, its uses whole again for the next, or the item with its last. A load gives its uses whole. An item holds one at most.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ValidationSideAttribute
files.Summary: Says which of an ability's checks a rule kind belongs among, and its picker offers it there alone. A kind that says none belongs among either.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ValueBreakdown
files.Summary: A run's stages, each with the value it took and gave and a note: what a combat log, a debugger and a test read of a hit. One is kept for each effect spec and filled again by each run.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ValuePipeline
files.Summary:
A value through ordered stages as it lands. An effect names one as its impact's calculation, as an Unreal effect names its execution calculation, so each hit goes through the stages a project writes once: the caster's bonuses, those that read the target, a critical roll, the target's reductions, a barrier; and what comes out lands. A new item that changes every hit is a stage, not an edit to each attack. Generic: the value is any number an impact lands with, a blow, a heal, a drain.

It isn't a Scaler asset. A scaler is a number worked out from its context, read wherever a number is; a pipeline transforms a value it's given, once, as it lands, with both sides known, and its stages can do what a number can't: roll once for the hit and keep it, route a part of it into a barrier, say what each did.

It runs for what an impact commits: an instant impact's hit, each tick of a periodic one. A lasting impact's value is read again as its attribute changes, so nothing runs it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ValueRun
files.Summary: What a stage reads in a run: the hit's carrier, its number context, and the breakdown, if one's kept.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ValueStep
files.Summary: One stage's part of a run: what it took and what it gave, and a note.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.WaitForAttributeTask
files.Summary: Waits for an attribute of its caster or its target to cross a value, as a berserk's next stage waits for its Health to fall under half. The value is read as it starts, at its ability's level; the attribute each step.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.WaitForEventTask
files.Summary: Waits for a gameplay event sent to its caster or its target, by its tag or one under it, as a combo's next stage waits for its hit to connect. The core's own events, as Impact Taken, come while it waits, as the core sends them where anything listens.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.WaitForTagTask
files.Summary: Waits for its caster or its target to gain a tag, or to lose it, as a stage waits for a stun to wear off. A tag already held counts as gained, and one not held as lost, so it waits for the state, not a change.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.WhenAllStagePolicy
files.Summary: Stage completes when ALL tasks complete.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.WhenAnyStagePolicy
files.Summary: Stage completes when ANY task completes. Cancels remaining tasks.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.WhenNStagePolicy
files.Summary: Stage completes when N tasks complete. Cancels remaining tasks.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.WhereItDiedRespawnPlace
files.Summary: Where the entity died.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.WorkerContext
files.Summary: Context passed to workers during validation and execution. Provides access to the system, attribute cache, and current change value.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.WorkerNumberKind
files.Summary:
A value a worker answers under a key: the number asks, and a worker that implements answers from what it knows, as how much health its effect's target has lost since the effect began. So work a number can't do alone goes to a worker, and the number reads the result: a curse whose every fourth tick deals a share of the damage its target took since it landed is one effect, with one worker.

It asks the workers of the effect whose number it is, about that application of the effect, or the caster's or the target's own workers. The first worker that answers the key gives the value. Where none answers, as where the number isn't an effect's or the entity has no such worker, it reads its .
